# Stellar X

# Get Started

# Sodero Ecosystem

Sodero connects robot design, simulation and operation on one controller. You describe the robot in Stellar Designer, run it on Stellar X with the built-in controllers, and drive it in NVIDIA Isaac Sim or on real motors through a gateway.

The same controller and application structure can be reused in simulation and on supported hardware. Before operating the physical robot, configure its gateway and verify actuator mapping, calibration, limits and sensor settings.

______________________________________________________________________

## Core Architecture

**Gateways separate controllers from hardware.** Controllers never talk to hardware directly. A gateway connects them to EtherCAT drives, to a robot in NVIDIA Isaac Sim, or to sensors, so the same controller and controller document can drive a simulated robot and a real one.

**One Station runs every node.** Gateways, controllers, navigation and your own modules run as nodes of one Station on Stellar X. They are connected through ports with defined interfaces, so built-in nodes and your own work together in the same way on every robot.

______________________________________________________________________

## From Design to the Real Robot

The Sodero ecosystem connects the entire process, from robot design and validation to physical deployment, into a single pipeline.

```
flowchart TB
    D["Design<br>Stellar Designer"] --> S["Compose<br>Stellar Station"]
    S --> V["Simulate<br>Isaac Sim + Isaac Bridge"]
    V --> R["Run<br>Stellar X + real hardware"]
    R -. "same controller,<br>EtherCAT gateway" .- V
```

**Design: Stellar Designer.** A web-based tool for defining your robot's kinematics, links, joints, wheels and actuator mapping, and the gateway that connects its actuators, without any hardware.

**Compose: Stellar Station.** The control center on the controller. Add gateways and controllers as nodes, connect their ports, load their design documents and start them, all in the browser.

**Simulate: NVIDIA Isaac Sim.** The Isaac Bridge extension connects a robot in Isaac Sim to the Station. The simulated robot is driven by the same controller and controller document as the real one, through a simulation gateway instead of an EtherCAT gateway.

**Run: Stellar X.** The motion controller with an EtherCAT master that runs the Station and its nodes. On the real robot, its EtherCAT gateway drives the servo drives, after you have checked the actuator mapping, calibration and limits on the hardware.

In simulation and on the real robot alike, you operate the robot from the same built-in controller UIs: **Motion Studio** for manipulators, **Strider** for mobile bases and **Articulation** for articulated and legged robots.

**Tip:** The Station, Stellar Designer and the controller UIs run in the browser and are served by Stellar X itself: connect a PC to the controller's network and open its address. Other software is installed only where you use it: Isaac Sim with the Isaac Bridge extension for simulation, an SSH client for the SSH workspace, and the Device Bridge on a computer next to its sensors.

**Sodero Cloud.** The same Stellar Station, design documents and controller UIs also run in Sodero Cloud, where robots are simulated in Robot Worlds in the browser instead of Isaac Sim on your PC. See the [Sodero Cloud manual](https://docs.sodero.io/sodero-cloud/latest/).

______________________________________________________________________

## Integration and Extensibility

Beyond controlling a single robot, Sodero works with your own programs and tools.

**Modules.** Package your own programs and install them on the Station. They run as nodes next to the built-in ones and use the same interfaces to command robots, read sensors and send navigation goals.

**SSH Workspace and the `sodero` CLI.** Every Station operation is available as a command that prints JSON, for scripts, CI pipelines and AI coding agents.

______________________________________________________________________

Continue with [Key Concepts](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/get_started/key_concepts/index.md), then follow the [Learning Path](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/tutorials/learning_path/index.md).

# Key Concepts

This page explains the building blocks you will meet everywhere in Stellar: the Station, nodes, ports, gateways, controllers and design documents. Read it once before you follow the [Learning Path](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/tutorials/learning_path/index.md); the rest of the documentation uses these terms without explaining them again.

______________________________________________________________________

## What Runs on Stellar X

```
flowchart TB
    subgraph SX ["Stellar X"]
        direction TB
        UI["Stellar Station<br>web page · port 80"]
        NS["Network Settings<br>web page · port 3000"]
        WS["SSH Workspace<br>ssh · port 2222"]
        RT["Real-time runtime<br>runs the Station's nodes"]
        UI --> RT
        WS --> RT
    end
    PC["Your PC<br>(browser, SSH, Isaac Sim)"] --> UI
    PC --> NS
    PC --> WS
    RT -- "EtherCAT" --> HW["Motors and drives"]
    RT -- "LAN" --> SIM["Isaac Sim<br>(simulated robot)"]
```

| Part                 | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Stellar Station**  | The web page of the controller (`http://ROBOT_ADDRESS`). You build the robot system as a graph of nodes, load their documents, start them and watch their logs.                                                  |
| **Network Settings** | A small page on port 3000 for the LAN address and SSH keys. See [Network Settings](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/hardware_setup/stellar_series/network_settings/index.md).                             |
| **SSH Workspace**    | A development environment on the controller with the `sodero` command-line tool, for scripts and AI coding agents. See [SSH Workspace](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/ssh_workspace/overview/index.md). |
| **Runtime**          | Runs the Station's nodes in real time.                                                                                                                                                                           |

______________________________________________________________________

## Station and Nodes

A **Station** is the complete robot system on one controller. It is a graph of **nodes**: each node is one program, such as a motor gateway, a robot controller, a camera or your own application.

When you click **Add node** on the Station page, you choose one of four node types:

| Type            | Purpose                                       | Built-in modules                                                                                                                  |
| --------------- | --------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Gateway**     | Connects simulation or hardware to the system | Actuator gateway, IMU gateway, Camera gateway                                                                                     |
| **Controller**  | Defines a robot unit and its control          | Motion Studio, Strider, Articulation, Localizer, Visual odometry, Navigator, and Legged locomotion (prepared with Sodero support) |
| **Compound**    | Combines several robot units into one system  | Your own compound modules                                                                                                         |
| **Application** | Defines robot behaviors and task logic        | Your own modules                                                                                                                  |

Most built-in nodes have an ID of the form `sodero.<kind>.<name>`. You choose the name; the kind comes from the module:

| Module                                | Node ID                                                                                    |
| ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Actuator gateway                      | `sodero.actuator_gateway.NAME`                                                             |
| Camera gateway                        | `sodero.camera_gateway.NAME`                                                               |
| IMU gateway                           | `sodero.imu_gateway.NAME`                                                                  |
| Motion Studio                         | `sodero.mmc.NAME`                                                                          |
| Strider                               | `sodero.mlc.NAME`                                                                          |
| Articulation                          | `sodero.amc.NAME`                                                                          |
| Visual odometry, Localizer, Navigator | `sodero.visual_odometry`, `sodero.localizer`, `sodero.navigator` (one of each per Station) |

The rules for `NAME` are in [Nodes and Connections › Node Types and Modules](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/station/nodes_and_connections/#node-types-and-modules).

______________________________________________________________________

## Ports and Connections

Nodes work together through **ports**. Every node card on the Station page lists two kinds:

- **REQUIRES**: a service the node needs from another node.
- **PROVIDES**: a service the node offers to other nodes.

You connect a required port to a compatible provided port by dragging between them. The most important connection is the **servo link** between a controller and its gateway:

```
flowchart TB
    S["Strider<br>sodero.mlc.jackal"] -- "servo_link" --> G["Actuator gateway<br>sodero.actuator_gateway.jackal"]
    G -- "simulation" --> I["Isaac Sim<br>robot 'jackal'"]
    G -. "or EtherCAT" .-> M["Real motors"]
```

| From (requires)                                   | To (provides)                           | Meaning                                       |
| ------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| Motion Studio, Strider, Articulation `servo_link` | Actuator gateway `servo_link`           | The controller drives the gateway's actuators |
| Localizer `camera`                                | Camera gateway `camera`                 | The localizer sees through this camera        |
| Localizer `odometry`                              | Strider `odometry` (or Visual odometry) | The localizer follows the robot's motion      |
| Navigator `localization`, `map`                   | Localizer `localization`, `map`         | Where the robot is, and the map to plan on    |
| Navigator `mobile_base`                           | Strider `mobile_base`                   | The base the navigator drives                 |

The Station only connects compatible ports, so a wrong connection is refused at once instead of failing later.

______________________________________________________________________

## Gateways: Simulation or Real Hardware

A **gateway** is the only node that talks to actuators. Controllers never touch hardware directly; they send commands through their gateway. That is why the same controller and controller document can drive a simulated robot and a real one: the gateway's document decides which. The real robot still needs its own checks of actuator mapping, calibration, limits and sensors.

| Hardware type of the `.gw` | Drives                                                                                          |
| -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Isaac Sim**              | A robot in **NVIDIA Isaac Sim** on a PC on the same network, through the Isaac Bridge extension |
| **EtherCAT**               | Real EtherCAT drives on the controller's EtherCAT port                                          |

**Names must match.** A simulation gateway finds its robot in Isaac Sim by name. The gateway's **Robot name** must be exactly the name of the robot's articulation prim in the Isaac Sim scene (for example `/World/jackal` for the robot name `jackal`). With a different name, the gateway keeps waiting and the robot never moves. See [Simulation Gateway](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/gateways/simulation/index.md).

______________________________________________________________________

## Design Documents

Actuator gateways and robot controllers are configured by a **design document**. You create documents with **Stellar Designer** (gateway documents with its **Gateway Designer**) and load them into nodes on the Station page.

| File    | Node             | Contents                                                  |
| ------- | ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.gw`   | Actuator gateway | Hardware type, actuators, EtherCAT or simulation settings |
| `.sdd`  | Motion Studio    | Manipulator: kinematics, dynamics, actuator mapping       |
| `.sddm` | Strider          | Mobile base: drive type, wheels, limits, actuator mapping |
| `.sdda` | Articulation     | Articulated robot: joints and actuator mapping            |

Camera and IMU gateways, visual odometry, the localizer and the navigator have no design document. They have **settings** that you edit in the node's inspector on the Station page ([Design Documents](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/station/design_documents/#4-settings-of-sensor-and-navigation-nodes)). The localizer and the navigator also use a **map bundle** (`.nav`): one file with the map of the site and their settings ([Load and Configure a Map](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/navigation/map_bundle/index.md)).

Your own programs are installed as **modules** (packages) on the [Modules](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/station/modules/index.md) page and run as nodes on the Station.

______________________________________________________________________

## Simulation First, Then Real

The recommended workflow follows the same order every time:

1. **Design** the robot in Stellar Designer (`.sdd`, `.sddm` or `.sdda`).
1. **Simulate**: add a simulation gateway and the controller on the Station, connect them, and drive the robot in Isaac Sim.
1. **Go real**: give the robot an EtherCAT gateway document for its drives. The controller, its document and your applications are reused. Before you operate the robot, verify the actuator mapping, calibration, limits and sensor settings on the hardware, as in [EtherCAT Mobile Base](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/tutorials/ethercat_mobile_base/index.md).

______________________________________________________________________

## Glossary

| Term            | Meaning                                                                                                                                                         |
| --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Station         | The robot system on one controller, shown as a node graph on the Station page                                                                                   |
| Node            | One program in the Station, such as a gateway, a controller, a sensor or your module                                                                            |
| Port            | A connection point of a node: REQUIRES (needs) or PROVIDES (offers)                                                                                             |
| Gateway         | A node that connects controllers to actuators or sensors, real or simulated                                                                                     |
| Controller      | A node of the Controller type: a robot controller, such as Motion Studio, Strider or Articulation, or a navigation node (Localizer, Visual odometry, Navigator) |
| Design document | The configuration file of an actuator gateway or a robot controller: `.gw`, `.sdd`, `.sddm`, `.sdda`                                                            |
| Map bundle      | A `.nav` file with the map of a site and the settings of the localizer and the navigator                                                                        |
| Module          | A program that runs as a node: built in, or your own package installed on the Modules page                                                                      |
| SDR             | A backup file of the whole Station: graph, documents and settings                                                                                               |
| World           | The simulated scene in Isaac Sim that the Station's simulation gateways connect to                                                                              |
| Isaac Bridge    | The Isaac Sim extension that connects the World to the Station                                                                                                  |

# Learning Path

The tutorials of this documentation build on each other: first connection, a simulated robot, navigation, then real motors. Follow them in this order, or start where your project is. The first hands-on tutorial is the [Quick Start](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/get_started/quick_start/index.md); its [Before You Start](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/get_started/quick_start/#before-you-start) section lists what to prepare.

```
flowchart TB
    A["1. Connect Stellar X"] --> B["2. Quick Start<br>simulated Jackal"]
    B --> C["3. Navigate in Simulation"]
    B --> D["4. Your own robot documents"]
    D --> E["5. EtherCAT Mobile Base<br>real motors"]
    C --> F["6. Extend and automate"]
    E --> F
```

# Quick Start

You will build a small robot system on Stellar X and drive a simulated **Clearpath Jackal** in NVIDIA Isaac Sim with Strider. It takes about 15 minutes once Stellar X is on your network and Isaac Sim with the Isaac Bridge extension is installed (see [Before You Start](#before-you-start)). You will:

1. add an actuator gateway and a Strider controller on Stellar Station,
1. load their design documents,
1. connect Isaac Sim, and
1. jog the robot from the browser.

```
flowchart TB
    B["Your browser<br>Stellar Station · Strider"]
    subgraph SX ["Stellar X"]
        S["Strider<br>sodero.mlc.jackal"] -- servo_link --> G["Actuator gateway<br>sodero.actuator_gateway.jackal"]
    end
    I["Isaac Sim + Isaac Bridge<br>robot /World/jackal"]
    B --> S
    G -- "LAN · TCP 53333–53335" --> I
```

______________________________________________________________________

## Before You Start

| You need                   | Details                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Stellar X                  | Powered on and reachable from your PC ([Stellar X › Network Configuration](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/hardware_setup/stellar_series/stellar_x/#4-network-configuration), [Network Settings](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/hardware_setup/stellar_series/network_settings/index.md)). In this guide its address is `192.168.60.18`, an example address on a lab network; use your controller's address instead, for example `10.0.0.1` on a direct cable. |
| A PC with NVIDIA Isaac Sim | Isaac Sim 6.0 with the Isaac Bridge 1.0.0 extension installed and enabled ([Install Isaac Bridge](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/virtual_simulation/extension_installation/index.md)), on the same network as Stellar X. In this guide its address is `192.168.60.20`.                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Example files              | [jackal.gw](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/get_started/quick_start/files/jackal.gw) (gateway), [jackal.sddm](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/get_started/quick_start/files/jackal.sddm) (Strider) and [jackal_warehouse.zip](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/get_started/quick_start/files/jackal_warehouse.zip) (Isaac Sim scene, 6 MB). Download all three and extract the scene.                                                                    |

The Isaac Sim PC must accept TCP connections from Stellar X on ports 53333–53335. Allow them in its firewall ([Install Isaac Bridge](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/virtual_simulation/extension_installation/#4-allow-the-ports-in-the-firewall)).

**Tip:** If you will continue with [Navigate in Simulation](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/navigation/simulation_tutorial/index.md), start Isaac Sim for this guide with the camera setting of its [Step 1](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/navigation/simulation_tutorial/#step-1-prepare-isaac-sim). Then you do not need to restart Isaac Sim later.

______________________________________________________________________

## Step 1: Add the Gateway

1. Open `http://192.168.60.18` in your browser.

1. Click **Add node**, choose **Gateway** ①, then **Actuator gateway** ② and click **Next** ③.

   Gateway › Actuator gateway

1. Name it `jackal` ① and click **Add node** ②.

______________________________________________________________________

## Step 2: Load the Gateway Document

1. Select the new node `sodero.actuator_gateway.jackal`. In its inspector, click the upload icon in **DEFINITION** (**Import .gw**).

1. On **From your PC** ①, choose `jackal.gw` ② and click **Import** ③.

1. In **TARGET**, click **Change** and set the two values:

   - **Robot name** ①: `jackal`. It must equal the robot's prim name in Isaac Sim (`/World/jackal`).
   - **Sim host** ②: the IP address of your Isaac Sim PC.

   Click **Done** ③.

   TARGET: ① Robot name ② Sim host ③ Done

If the robot name differs from the prim name in Isaac Sim, the gateway waits forever and the robot never moves.

______________________________________________________________________

## Step 3: Add Strider and Connect It

1. Click **Add node**, choose **Controller** ① › **Strider** ② and click **Next** ③. Name it `jackal` and click **Add node**.
1. Select `sodero.mlc.jackal` and click the upload icon in **DEFINITION** (**Import .sddm**). On **From your PC** ①, choose `jackal.sddm` ② and click **Import** ③.
1. Connect the two nodes: drag from the Strider's `servo_link` (left edge) to the gateway's `servo_link` (right edge), or click **Auto-connect** next to `servo_link` in the Strider's inspector.

The gateway and Strider connected through servo_link

______________________________________________________________________

## Step 4: Play the Scene in Isaac Sim

1. Open `jackal_warehouse.usd` in Isaac Sim (**File › Open**). The scene contains a Clearpath Jackal at `/World/jackal` and a Clearpath Dingo at `/World/dingo_d` in a warehouse.
1. Press **Play**.
1. Open **Window › Isaac Bridge**. It shows the ports as **serving** and `jackal … bound, 4 DOF`.

Isaac Bridge status: ① ports serving ② robots bound ③ cameras ④ Rescan

**Tip:** To use your own robot instead, prepare its scene as described in [Prepare the Robot](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/virtual_simulation/robot_setup/index.md): its articulation prim name is its robot name, and its joints, in order, are the gateway's actuators.

______________________________________________________________________

## Step 5: Start the Nodes

1. Select the gateway and click **Start node**. Wait until its state is **Operating**.
1. Select the Strider and click **Start node**.

In the gateway's **LOGS** (stream **Gateway events**) you see the connection to Isaac Sim:

```
Gateway sodero.actuator_gateway.jackal starting: simulation, 4 actuator(s), 1.0 ms cycle.
Simulation: robot 'jackal', simulator at 192.168.60.20; waiting for it to start.
Simulator connected.
```

______________________________________________________________________

## Step 6: Jog the Robot with Strider

1. In the Strider node's inspector, click **Strider** in **CONTROL**. Strider opens in a new tab.
1. Open the **Drive** page (gamepad icon in the left rail).
1. Under **Drive Mode**, click **Twist** ①.
1. Under **Servo / Safety**, switch **Servo On** ②.
1. Press and hold **Forward (W)** on the pad ⑤. The robot drives while you hold the button and stops when you release it. **Turn Left (A)**, **Turn Right (D)** and **Backward (S)** work the same way.

Strider's Drive page: ① Twist ② Servo On ③ Live switch for the keyboard ④ speed limits ⑤ drive pad ⑥⑦ stop and emergency stop ⑧ readiness

**Tip:** Switch on **Live** ③ in **Manual Drive** to drive with the keyboard: **W**/**S** forward and back, **A**/**D** turn, **Space** stops.

The simulated Jackal after a short drive and turn

When you are done, switch the servo off and click **Idle** under **Drive Mode**.

______________________________________________________________________

| Move from simulation to real motors                        | [EtherCAT Mobile Base](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/tutorials/ethercat_mobile_base/index.md), [EtherCAT Gateway](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/gateways/ethercat/index.md)              |
| Let an AI coding agent do it for you                       | [AI Coding Agents](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/ssh_workspace/ai_agents/index.md)                                                                                                                 |
# Hardware and Network

# Stellar X

This guide takes you from unboxing and hardware assembly to the first network connection between Stellar X and your PC.

______________________________________________________________________

## 1. What's in the Box

Check that your package includes the following components. If anything is missing, contact [our support team](https://www.sodero.io/contact).

Stellar X Main Unit

24V Power Adapter

Power Cable

______________________________________________________________________

## 2. Device Overview

The network and power ports are on the rear panel.

Rear panel: ① Eth1 ② Eth2 ③ EtherCAT Out ④ 24V DC In

| Port                | Initial setting                                        | How to change it                                                                                                                                                | Use                                                                                |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **1. Eth1**         | Static address `10.0.0.1`, subnet mask `255.255.255.0` | On the [Network Settings](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/hardware_setup/stellar_series/network_settings/index.md) page: DHCP or another static address | First connection with a cable from your PC; afterwards your office or lab network  |
| **2. Eth2**         | DHCP                                                   | Not changed by the Network Settings page                                                                                                                        | A router or switch that assigns addresses by DHCP                                  |
| **3. EtherCAT Out** | No IP address                                          | —                                                                                                                                                               | EtherCAT master output. Connect it to the **IN** port of the first EtherCAT drive. |
| **4. 24V DC In**    | —                                                      | —                                                                                                                                                               | Power input                                                                        |

______________________________________________________________________

## 3. Hardware Setup & Power On

Follow these steps in order to prevent electrical damage.

1. **Prepare the Adapter:** Connect the power cable to the 24V power adapter. **Do not plug it into the wall outlet yet.**

1. **Connect to Stellar X:** Insert the adapter's output cable into the **24V DC In** port on the unit.

   To prevent **electrical arcing (sparks)** or connection issues, always connect the cable to the **Stellar X unit first**, and *then* plug the power adapter into the wall.

   The connector has a small guide notch inside. If it doesn't slide in easily, **gently rotate the cable** until the notch aligns with the port.

   Aligning the connector notch

1. **Secure the Connection:** Once the connector is fully inserted, hand-tighten its metal nut so that it stays locked in place.

   Securing the locking nut

1. **Power Up:** Plug the power cable into a wall outlet. Stellar X powers on automatically and takes about 1 minute to start up.

______________________________________________________________________

## 4. Network Configuration

Your PC must be on the same subnet as Stellar X.

1. **Physical Connection:** Connect an Ethernet (LAN) cable to **Eth1 (Port 1)** on the Stellar X unit and the other end to your PC's LAN port.

   Connecting to Eth1

1. **Configure Your PC:** Eth1 starts with the static address `10.0.0.1`, so set your PC to a static IP in the same subnet (e.g., `10.0.0.2`).

   Avoid using `10.0.0.1` for your PC, as this will cause an IP conflict.

   - **For Ubuntu Users:**

     1. Go to **Settings > Network**.
     1. Click the **gear icon** next to your wired connection.
     1. Select the **IPv4** tab and choose **Manual**.
     1. Set Address: `10.0.0.2` / Netmask: `255.255.255.0`.
     1. Click **Apply**.

   - **For Windows Users:**

     1. Go to **Settings > Network & Internet > Ethernet**.
     1. Find **IP assignment** and click **Edit**.
     1. Select **Manual**, toggle **IPv4 On**, and enter:
        - IP address: `10.0.0.2`
        - Subnet mask: `255.255.255.0`
     1. Click **Save**.

1. **Verify the Connection:** Open your preferred web browser (Chrome, Edge, etc.) and type the following into the address bar: `http://10.0.0.1`

1. **Success!** If **Stellar Station** appears, you are ready to start your project. Continue with the [Quick Start](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/get_started/quick_start/index.md).

   Stellar Station with an example robot system

   To change Eth1's address or to connect it to your office network, use the [Network Settings](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/hardware_setup/stellar_series/network_settings/index.md) page on port 3000. The rest of this documentation uses the example address `192.168.60.18` for Stellar X; replace it with your controller's address, for example `10.0.0.1` while you use the direct cable.

# Network Settings

Stellar X serves a small settings page on **port 3000**. Use it for the two things you need before anything else:

- the IP address of the controller's LAN port **Eth1**, and
- SSH access to the controller's [SSH workspace](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/ssh_workspace/overview/index.md).

Open the page from any computer on the same network:

```
http://ROBOT_ADDRESS:3000
```

In this guide the controller's address is `192.168.60.18`, an example address on a lab network, so the page is `http://192.168.60.18:3000`. Replace it with your controller's address.

**Initial address: static `10.0.0.1`.** Eth1 starts with the static address `10.0.0.1` (subnet mask `255.255.255.0`). To reach it the first time, connect your PC with a cable and give the PC a static address in the same subnet, such as `10.0.0.2` ([Stellar X](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/hardware_setup/stellar_series/stellar_x/#4-network-configuration)). Then open `http://10.0.0.1:3000` and change the address under [IP Configuration](#1-ip-configuration).

The page needs no sign-in: anyone on the same network can change the address and register SSH keys. Connect Stellar X only to networks you trust.

The Network Settings page

Stellar Station itself is served on the standard web port: `http://ROBOT_ADDRESS` (port 80). Port 3000 is only for these settings.

______________________________________________________________________

## 1. IP Configuration

The **IP CONFIGURATION** card shows and changes the address of Eth1. The page shows no port name; every value on the card belongs to Eth1.

Current address and IP assignment

| No. | Item            | Description                                                                                                                                                                 |
| --- | --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | Current address | The address Eth1 has now, how it got it (**DHCP** or **Static**), the subnet mask and the port's MAC address. **Connected** means a cable is plugged in and the link is up. |
| 2   | **DHCP**        | The router assigns the address. This is the simplest setup on an office or lab network.                                                                                     |
| 3   | **Static**      | You enter the address yourself. Use it for a direct cable between your PC and the controller, or on a network without a DHCP server.                                        |
| 4   | **Apply**       | Applies the selection. Nothing changes until you click it.                                                                                                                  |

### Set a Static Address

Static address

1. Click **Static** ①. The card shows **IP ADDRESS** and **SUBNET MASK**.
1. Enter the new address in **IP ADDRESS** ②. The subnet mask ③ is fixed to `255.255.255.0`.
1. Click **Apply** ④.

After **Apply**, the controller moves to the new address and the page stops answering at the old one. Open `http://NEW_ADDRESS:3000` to continue.

Your PC must be on the same subnet to reach the new address. For example, after setting `10.0.0.1` on a direct cable, give your PC a static address such as `10.0.0.2` with mask `255.255.255.0`.

**Automatic rollback.** If the new setting cannot be applied, or no address comes up (for example **DHCP** is selected but no DHCP server answers), the controller restores its previous settings by itself and the page reports what happened.

### Notes

- The page changes **Eth1 only**. Eth2 keeps using DHCP. The EtherCAT port is reserved for EtherCAT devices; it never gets an IP address and is not shown here ([Stellar X › Device Overview](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/hardware_setup/stellar_series/stellar_x/#2-device-overview)).
- No default gateway is configured. Stellar X works on the local network and does not need Internet access.
- With **DHCP**, find the controller's address in your router's client list; its host name is `stellar-x`.

______________________________________________________________________

## 2. SSH Access

The **SSH ACCESS** card controls who can sign in to the controller's SSH workspace. The workspace accepts SSH keys only; there is no password sign-in.

SSH workspace status, registered keys and key registration

| No. | Item               | Description                                                                         |
| --- | ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | Connection command | The exact command to connect, with **Copy**. **Running** means the workspace is up. |
| 2   | Operating system   | Shows the key command for **Windows** (PowerShell) or **macOS · Linux**.            |
| 3   | Key command        | Creates a key on your computer if it has none, then prints its public key.          |
| 4   | Public key box     | Paste the printed line here. It starts with `ssh-ed25519`.                          |
| 5   | **Add key**        | Registers the key. It appears under **REGISTERED KEYS**.                            |

### Register a Computer

1. Select your operating system ②, click **Copy** ③ and run the command in a terminal on your computer.

   ```
   [ -f ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub ] || { mkdir -p ~/.ssh && ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -N "" -f ~/.ssh/id_ed25519; }; cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub
   ```

   ```
   if (!(Test-Path $HOME\.ssh\id_ed25519.pub)) { mkdir $HOME\.ssh -Force | Out-Null; ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f $HOME\.ssh\id_ed25519 }; Get-Content $HOME\.ssh\id_ed25519.pub | Set-Clipboard; Get-Content $HOME\.ssh\id_ed25519.pub
   ```

   On Windows the command also copies the key to the clipboard. When `ssh-keygen` asks for a passphrase, press Enter twice to create the key without one.

1. Paste the printed line into the box ④ and click **Add key** ⑤.

1. Click **Copy** next to the connection command ① and run it:

   ```
   ssh -p 2222 sodero@192.168.60.18
   ```

To revoke access, click the trash icon next to a key under **REGISTERED KEYS**. The computer can no longer sign in; files in the workspace are kept.

Paste only the **public** key (the `.pub` file). The page refuses private keys and keys with options.

Each person or computer should have its own key. The key's comment (for example `user@laptop`) is shown in the list, so you can tell the keys apart.

Continue with [SSH Workspace](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/ssh_workspace/overview/index.md) to learn what you can do once you are connected.

# Stop Controls

A robot on Stellar X can be stopped in several ways: buttons in the controller UIs and the test console, automatic stops of the gateway, and the emergency stop that you wire yourself. This page compares them, so that you know what each one does before real motors move.

**On-screen buttons are not emergency stops.** They are software functions of the controllers and the gateway, and they act only while the browser, the network, Stellar X and the drives work. Every robot with real motors needs a hardware emergency stop that removes motor power or triggers the drives' safe torque off (STO), wired as the drive manufacturer describes. Keep it within reach whenever the motors are powered.

______________________________________________________________________

## 1. Hardware Emergency Stop and STO

The hardware emergency stop and the drives' STO inputs are part of your machine, not of Stellar X. How they stop the motors depends on your wiring and on the drives. While they are active, the drives cannot be enabled: the gateway reports *Servo ON failed: drive … did not enable* ([EtherCAT Gateway › Troubleshooting](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/gateways/ethercat/#6-troubleshooting)). After you release them, switch the servo on again in the UI.

______________________________________________________________________

## 2. Stops in the UIs

The UIs are described in Operate Robots: [Strider](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/controllers/strider/index.md), [Motion Studio](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/controllers/motion_studio/index.md) and [Articulation](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/controllers/articulation/index.md); the test console in [Test Console](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/gateways/test_console/index.md).

| Control                                                                                            | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Servo afterwards | To continue                                                                                                              |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **E-STOP** (Strider, top bar)                                                                      | Cancels manual driving and the navigation goal and sets the wheel speeds to zero at once. The drives stay enabled and hold zero speed. The stop latches.                                                     | On               | **Clear E-Stop** (the base switches to **Idle**), then **Twist**                                                         |
| **Stop Motion**, **Stop (Space)**, releasing a pad button (Strider, Drive page)                    | Ends manual driving (and, for **Stop Motion**, a navigation goal). The base slows down at the acceleration limits of its document.                                                                           | On               | Drive again                                                                                                              |
| Releasing a jog button or **Hold to move** (Motion Studio)                                         | The arm slows down over a short ramp and holds its position.                                                                                                                                                 | On               | —                                                                                                                        |
| **Stop** (Articulation, top bar)                                                                   | Switches the servo off and latches a stop.                                                                                                                                                                   | Off              | **Clear stop**, then **Servo on**                                                                                        |
| **Servo Off** / **Servo off** / **Servo OFF** (Strider, Motion Studio, Articulation, test console) | Disables the drives. The motors no longer hold: a base rolls out, and a joint without a brake can fall. Whether a motor brake engages depends on the drive's configuration.                                  | Off              | Switch the servo on                                                                                                      |
| **EMERGENCY STOP** (test console)                                                                  | Sends a quick stop to every drive of the gateway and switches the servo off. How a drive slows down depends on its quick stop settings. While it is active, **Servo ON** and **Fault Reset** have no effect. | Off              | Click it again to release it, then **Servo ON**. If a drive does not enable again, end the test and restart the gateway. |

Motion Studio has no on-screen emergency stop. Use the hardware emergency stop, or switch the servo off where the arm can safely lose its holding torque.

**A closed tab does not stop the robot.** Closing a UI tab or losing the network connection is not a stop command. Strider stops manual driving within about a second, but a navigation goal continues. In Motion Studio and the [test console](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/gateways/test_console/index.md), a motion that is running when the browser loses the page can continue. Stop the motion before you leave a UI, and use the hardware emergency stop when a UI does not respond.

______________________________________________________________________

## 3. Automatic Stops

| Situation                                                                          | What happens                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | To continue                                                                 |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A controller stops sending commands while the servo is on                          | The gateway keeps the last command for 3 s, then switches the servo off (*No commands from the robot controller for 3.0 s: servo turned OFF for safety.*).                                                                              | Start the controller and switch the servo on                                |
| EtherCAT communication is lost                                                     | Each drive reacts as its own communication watchdog is configured. The gateway reports *EtherCAT communication lost* in **Gateway events** with the likely cause, and asks for a restart if communication does not come back by itself. | Fix the cable or the drive's power, then restart the gateway                |
| A drive reports a fault                                                            | The gateway reports the fault in **Gateway events**.                                                                                                                                                                                    | Fix the cause, **Fault Reset** or **Error Reset**, then switch the servo on |
| Motion Studio: a joint limit, a speed or torque limit, or a collision              | Protective stop: the arm holds its position with the servo on ([Manipulator › Robot System Parameters](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/tutorials/stellar_designer/manipulator/#step-2-robot-system-parameters)).                | **Error Reset**                                                             |
| Motion Studio: no feedback from the gateway, or a critical drive fault             | Emergency stop: the controller requests a quick stop and the servo switches off.                                                                                                                                                        | Stop and start the Motion Studio node                                       |
| Articulation: feedback older than 100 ms, or no new target for 200 ms (by default) | The servo switches off and a stop latches.                                                                                                                                                                                              | **Clear stop**, then **Servo on**                                           |
| Strider: no manual command for about 1 s                                           | The base slows to a stop.                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Drive again                                                                 |

______________________________________________________________________

## 4. Before You Power Real Motors

1. Wire and test the hardware emergency stop and the drives' STO.
1. Lift wheels off the ground, or keep the axes clear of their end stops.
1. Check each actuator alone with the [test console](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/gateways/test_console/index.md), at low speed.
1. Start the controller with low limits, and keep someone at the emergency stop.
# Stellar Station

# Stellar Station Overview

**Stellar Station** is the control center of Stellar X. In a web browser you build the robot system as a graph of nodes (gateways, controllers, sensors, navigation and your own modules), load their design documents, start them, and watch their state and logs. The controller UIs (Motion Studio, Strider and Articulation) and Stellar Designer open from the Station as well.

Open the Station from any computer on the controller's network:

```
http://ROBOT_ADDRESS
```

In this guide the address is `192.168.60.18`. On the controller's own network the Station needs no sign-in. Use a recent version of Chrome or Edge.

If you do not know the controller's address yet, see [Network Settings](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/hardware_setup/stellar_series/network_settings/index.md).

______________________________________________________________________

## 1. Screen Layout

The Runtime page of Stellar Station

| No. | Item                      | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| --- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | **Runtime** / **Modules** | The two pages of the Station. **Runtime** is the node graph shown here; **Modules** lists the available modules and installs your own ([Modules](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/station/modules/index.md)). |
| 2   | **LIVE** and uptime       | The Station is running, and how long it has been running.                                                                                                                                                            |
| 3   | Save state                | **Saved** / **Saving…**. Every change to the graph is saved to the controller automatically. If a save fails, the label turns into **Retry save**.                                                                   |
| 4   | **Filter**                | Shows only nodes of a type (Gateway, Controller, Compound, Application) or a status. Nodes connected to a match stay visible but dimmed.                                                                             |
| 5   | **Load SDR**              | Replaces the whole Station with an `.sdr` file ([Backup and Restore](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/station/backup_restore/index.md)).                                                                      |
| 6   | **Export SDR**            | Downloads the whole Station as an `.sdr` file.                                                                                                                                                                       |
| 7   | **Add node**              | Adds a gateway, controller, compound or application node ([Nodes and Connections](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/station/nodes_and_connections/index.md)).                                                  |
| 8   | **Start all nodes**       | Starts or stops every node in dependency order ([Running Nodes](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/station/running_nodes/index.md)).                                                                            |
| 9   | **Resources**             | CPU, memory and GPU load of the controller.                                                                                                                                                                          |
| 10  | Node card                 | One node of the graph, with its ports and its state.                                                                                                                                                                 |
| 11  | Canvas controls           | Zoom out, zoom level and zoom in, **Fit view**, **Auto layout**, and collapse or expand all node cards. Drag the empty canvas to move the view.                                                                      |
| 12  | Inspector                 | Details of the selected node: its state, controls, design document, connections and logs. The button at the right end of the toolbar shows or hides it.                                                              |

**Tip:** Right-click the empty canvas to add a node directly, and right-click a node for its actions (start, stop, open its UI, delete).

______________________________________________________________________

## 2. Resources

Click **Resources** to see the controller's load. **View details** opens the system monitor.

Resource usage

System monitor

The bars turn amber at 70 % and red at 85 %. Stellar X has no GPU, so GPU shows **—**.

______________________________________________________________________

## 3. Theme

Click the Stellar mark at the top left and choose **Theme** › **Midnight** (dark) or **Twilight** (light).

______________________________________________________________________

## 4. What You Do on the Station

A typical robot system is built in this order. Each step has its own page.

```
flowchart TB
    A["Add nodes<br>gateway + controller"] --> B["Load design documents<br>.gw · .sdd · .sddm · .sdda"]
    B --> C["Connect ports<br>servo_link"]
    C --> D["Start nodes"]
    D --> E["Operate<br>Motion Studio · Strider · Articulation"]
```

| Step                                                                     | Page                                                                                                    |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Add nodes and connect their ports                                        | [Nodes and Connections](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/station/nodes_and_connections/index.md) |
| Load or edit the documents of the nodes                                  | [Design Documents](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/station/design_documents/index.md)           |
| Start and stop nodes, read their state and logs, open the controller UIs | [Running Nodes](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/station/running_nodes/index.md)                 |
| Install your own programs                                                | [Modules](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/station/modules/index.md)                             |
| Back up, restore or copy the whole Station                               | [Backup and Restore](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/station/backup_restore/index.md)           |

For a complete walkthrough with a simulated robot, follow the [Quick Start](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/get_started/quick_start/index.md).

______________________________________________________________________

## 5. Pages Served by Stellar X

| Address                            | What it is                                                                                                           |
| ---------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `http://ROBOT_ADDRESS`             | Stellar Station, and Stellar Designer when opened from a node                                                        |
| `http://ROBOT_ADDRESS:8081/...`    | Controller UIs (Motion Studio, Strider, Articulation) and module UIs; open them from their nodes on the Station page |
| `http://ROBOT_ADDRESS:3000`        | [Network Settings](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/hardware_setup/stellar_series/network_settings/index.md)  |
| `ssh -p 2222 sodero@ROBOT_ADDRESS` | [SSH Workspace](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/ssh_workspace/overview/index.md)                             |

Anyone who can reach the controller's network can open the Station and command the robot. Keep Stellar X on a trusted network.

# Nodes and Connections

A Station is a graph of **nodes** connected through **ports**. This page shows how to add nodes, connect them, and rename or delete them. See [Key Concepts](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/get_started/key_concepts/index.md) for what the node types mean.

______________________________________________________________________

## 1. Add a Node

1. Click **Add node** in the toolbar (or right-click the empty canvas).

1. Choose a node type ①, select a module ② and click **Next** ③.

   Gateway › Actuator gateway

1. Enter a node name ① and click **Add node** ②. You can rename the node later in the inspector.

   Naming the node

The new node appears on the canvas in the **Planned** state. It is saved with the graph, but nothing runs until you start it.

### Node Types and Modules

| Type            | Module                   | Typical use                                                 |
| --------------- | ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Gateway**     | Actuator gateway         | Motors and drives, real (EtherCAT) or simulated (Isaac Sim) |
|                 | IMU gateway              | IMU and foot-contact data                                   |
|                 | Camera gateway           | An RGB-D camera                                             |
| **Controller**  | Motion Studio            | Manipulators                                                |
|                 | Strider                  | Wheeled mobile bases                                        |
|                 | Articulation             | Articulated robots with direct joint control                |
|                 | Localizer                | Map-based localization (one per Station)                    |
|                 | Visual odometry          | Camera-based odometry (one per Station)                     |
|                 | Navigator                | Path planning and goal following (one per Station)          |
| **Compound**    | Your compound modules    | Several robot units combined into one system                |
| **Application** | Your application modules | Robot behaviors and task logic                              |

The module sets the node's ID: an actuator gateway named `jackal` becomes `sodero.actuator_gateway.jackal`. The IDs of all built-in modules are listed in [Key Concepts › Station and Nodes](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/get_started/key_concepts/#station-and-nodes).

**Legged locomotion** and **Visual odometry** need preparation that this documentation does not cover step by step. Legged locomotion runs a walking policy made for your robot, whose joint names and order must match the robot's Articulation document. Visual odometry needs a calibrated camera, and an IMU for walking robots. This documentation describes their connections and settings; ask Sodero support before you use them on your robot.

Modules marked **SODERO** are built in. Modules you installed on the [Modules](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/station/modules/index.md) page are marked **CUSTOM** and appear under the type they declare. Each type also lists a **… subsystem** entry (*Empty draft subsystem*): it adds an empty placeholder node with no program behind it, for sketching a system, and that node cannot be started.

Choosing a controller module: ① Controller ② Strider ③ Next (the list scrolls)

**Name rules.** Gateway names have at most 64 characters. They are converted to lowercase, and every character other than `a`–`z`, `0`–`9`, `_` and `-` becomes `_`. Controller names (Motion Studio, Strider, Articulation) have at most 24 characters, start with a lowercase letter and use only lowercase letters, digits and `_`. Names of nodes from your own modules have at most 60 characters, start with a letter or digit and use letters, digits, `_`, `.` and `-`. The Localizer, Visual odometry and Navigator have fixed names.

**Tip:** Give a robot's gateway and controller the same name, for example `sodero.actuator_gateway.jackal` and `sodero.mlc.jackal`. The graph stays easy to read, and **Auto-connect** finds the right partner.

______________________________________________________________________

## 2. The Node Card

A gateway and a Strider connected through servo_link

| Part             | Meaning                                                                                                                                                            |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Title and module | The node ID and its module, for example `sodero.actuator_gateway.jackal` / Stellar actuator gateway. A running controller shows a link to its UI here.             |
| **REQUIRES n/m** | Ports this node needs from other nodes: connected / total. Required ports sit on the left edge of the card.                                                        |
| **PROVIDES n/m** | Ports this node offers: ports with at least one connection / total. They sit on the right edge.                                                                    |
| Status           | The node's state, such as **Planned**, **Operating** or **Error** ([Running Nodes](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/station/running_nodes/#3-node-states)). |

The card border has the color of the node type: orange for gateways, blue-violet for controllers, purple for compounds and mint for applications.

______________________________________________________________________

## 3. Connect Ports

Connect a required port to a provided port of another node. There are three ways:

- **Drag** from one port dot to another. While you drag, compatible ports pulse blue and incompatible ones turn red.
- **Click** one port, then the other.
- In the inspector of the node that requires the port, click **Auto-connect** next to the port. The Station picks the matching provider.

The Station accepts a connection only when the two ports are on different nodes, one requires and the other provides, and both use the same contract (the interface type shown under the port name in the inspector, for example `api.actuator.servo.v1`). It also enforces the system structure:

- Only a **controller** may use a gateway.
- An **application** uses controllers or compounds, never gateways directly.
- An actuator gateway serves one robot controller (Motion Studio, Strider or Articulation) at a time.

### Common Connections

| Node (requires)                      | Port                                 | Connect to (provides)                                          |
| ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Motion Studio, Strider, Articulation | `servo_link`                         | Actuator gateway `servo_link`                                  |
| Legged locomotion                    | `servo`, `imu`                       | Articulation `articulation`, IMU gateway `imu`                 |
| Localizer                            | `camera`, `odometry`                 | Camera gateway `camera`; Strider or Visual odometry `odometry` |
| Visual odometry                      | `camera`, `imu` (optional)           | Camera gateway `camera`; IMU gateway `imu`                     |
| Navigator                            | `mobile_base`, `localization`, `map` | Strider `mobile_base`; Localizer `localization` and `map`      |

To remove a connection, select the node and click **Disconnect** next to the port in the inspector.

**Tip:** A Motion Studio node can drive actuators of several gateways. Click **+ Gateway link** in its inspector to add another `servo_link` port.

______________________________________________________________________

## 4. The Inspector

Click a node to open its inspector. The sections depend on the node type.

A gateway node: ① Start node ② its document ③ import ④ Gateway Designer ⑤ TARGET ⑥ CONNECTION ⑦ LOGS

A Strider node: ① Start node ② its controller UI ③ its document ④ Stellar Designer ⑤ import. The box shows the gateway it drives.

| Section        | Contents                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Header         | Node name (pencil icon to rename), module, state, and **Start node** / **Stop node**                                                                                                                                                                                |
| **CONTROL**    | Buttons that open the node's tool: **Stellar Motion Studio**, **Strider**, **Articulation** for controllers; **Test Stellar Gateway** for gateways. They unlock once the node runs.                                                                                 |
| **DEFINITION** | The node's design document: file name and when it was imported, **Edit Stellar Designer** / **Edit Stellar Gateway Designer**, and the upload icon to import a file ([Design Documents](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/station/design_documents/index.md)) |
| **TARGET**     | Simulation gateways only: the robot name in Isaac Sim and the **Sim host** ([Simulation Gateway](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/gateways/simulation/index.md))                                                                                             |
| Settings       | Camera, IMU, visual odometry, localizer, navigator and legged locomotion nodes: their settings form                                                                                                                                                                 |
| **CONNECTION** | Requires and Provides ports with their contracts, **Auto-connect** and **Disconnect**                                                                                                                                                                               |
| **LOGS**       | Output and events of the node ([Running Nodes](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/station/running_nodes/#5-logs))                                                                                                                                              |

______________________________________________________________________

## 5. Rename and Delete

- **Rename:** stop the node, then click the pencil icon next to the node name in the inspector.
- **Delete:** stop the node, then right-click it and choose **Delete node**. The node and its connections are removed from the graph.

Right-click menu of a node

Delete confirmation

Deleting a node cannot be undone. Export the Station first if you may need the node again ([Backup and Restore](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/station/backup_restore/index.md)).

______________________________________________________________________

## 6. Find Nodes in a Large Graph

- **Filter** shows nodes of one type or status.
- **Fit view** zooms to show every node; **Auto layout** arranges the nodes by their connections.
- The **N issues** chip at the left of the toolbar lists problems such as unconnected required ports; **Locate** jumps to the node.

Filter by node type and status

# Design Documents

Gateways and robot controllers are configured by **design documents**. You create them in Stellar Designer, load them into nodes on the Station, and edit them later directly from the node.

| File    | Node             | Edited with                                                                                                                                           |
| ------- | ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.gw`   | Actuator gateway | Stellar Gateway Designer ([Gateway Designer](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/gateways/gateway_designer/index.md))                             |
| `.sdd`  | Motion Studio    | Stellar Designer, manipulator editor ([Manipulator](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/tutorials/stellar_designer/manipulator/index.md))         |
| `.sddm` | Strider          | Stellar Designer, mobile robot editor ([Mobile Robot](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/tutorials/stellar_designer/mobile_robot/index.md))      |
| `.sdda` | Articulation     | Stellar Designer, articulation editor ([Articulated Robot](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/tutorials/stellar_designer/articulation/index.md)) |

Cameras, IMUs, visual odometry, the localizer and the navigator have no design document. They have **settings** that you edit in the node's inspector (see [Settings of Sensor and Navigation Nodes](#4-settings-of-sensor-and-navigation-nodes)).

Every new gateway or controller node starts with an empty document of its type, so you can either import a finished file or build the document from scratch with **Edit Stellar Designer** (**Edit Stellar Gateway Designer** for gateways).

______________________________________________________________________

## 1. Import a Document

1. Stop the node if it is running.
1. Select the node. In the inspector's **DEFINITION** section, click the upload icon (**Import .gw**, **Import .sdd**, **Import .sddm** or **Import .sdda**).
1. On **From your PC** ①, drop the file or click **Choose file**. The chosen file appears ②; click **Import** ③.

Importing a gateway document

The **DEFINITION** section then shows the file name and *imported just now*.

An import **replaces the whole document** of the node. Export the Station first if you may need the previous version ([Backup and Restore](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/station/backup_restore/index.md)).

**My Library**, **Workspace Library** and **Sodero Assets** list files stored in Sodero Cloud. They need a Sodero account and Internet access. On a controller without Internet access, use **From your PC**.

______________________________________________________________________

## 2. Edit a Document in Stellar Designer

Click **Edit Stellar Designer** (controllers) or **Edit Stellar Gateway Designer** (gateways) in the **DEFINITION** section. Stellar Designer opens in a new browser tab with the node's document. The breadcrumb at the top shows the node and the file, for example `sodero.mlc.jackal / jackal.sddm`.

- **Stop the node before you edit its document.** While the node runs, the Station refuses to save.
- Your edits are saved back to the node automatically. In an Articulation document, click **Save configuration**.
- The arrow at the left of the breadcrumb returns to the Station.

The editors are described in [Stellar Designer](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/tutorials/stellar_designer/introduction/index.md) and [Gateway Designer](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/gateways/gateway_designer/index.md).

______________________________________________________________________

## 3. Point a Simulation Gateway at Its Robot

A simulation gateway also needs to know **which robot** in Isaac Sim it drives and **where** Isaac Sim runs. Select the gateway and click **Change** in its **TARGET** section:

Robot name and Sim host of a simulation gateway

| No. | Field          | Value                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| --- | -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | **Robot name** | The name of the robot's articulation prim in the Isaac Sim scene, for example `jackal` for `/World/jackal`                                                                                                                                      |
| 2   | **Sim host**   | The IP address of the computer that runs Isaac Sim. A simulator address set for the controller replaces it ([Addresses Set for the Controller](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/gateways/simulation/#addresses-set-for-the-controller)). |
| 3   | **Done**       | Saves both values. They take effect when the gateway starts next time.                                                                                                                                                                          |

**The robot name must match exactly.** The gateway finds its robot in Isaac Sim by name only. If the names differ, the gateway keeps waiting for the simulator and the robot never moves. See [Simulation Gateway](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/gateways/simulation/index.md).

______________________________________________________________________

## 4. Settings of Sensor and Navigation Nodes

Camera gateways, IMU gateways, visual odometry, the localizer, the navigator and legged locomotion are configured with settings forms in their inspector, and on a full-page **Settings** view that opens from the node card.

- Stop the node, change the values, then click **Save settings**. **Reload** discards unsaved changes.
- The localizer and the navigator share their settings with the map bundle. They can be saved only while the localizer, the navigator and visual odometry are stopped.
- The localizer's map is loaded with **Upload .nav** ([Load and Configure a Map](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/navigation/map_bundle/index.md)). The navigator uses the same bundle.

The same settings can be read and written from the SSH workspace with `sodero navigation get` and `sodero navigation apply` ([sodero CLI](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/ssh_workspace/sodero_cli/index.md)).

______________________________________________________________________

## 5. Rules for Documents

- A Motion Studio, Strider or Articulation document names the gateway it drives and the gateway's actuator indices (zero-based). Connect the node's `servo_link` to that same gateway.
- A simulation gateway document has `hardware.type: simulation`. Its robot name and **Sim host** are set on the node ([section 3](#3-point-a-simulation-gateway-at-its-robot)).
- The gateway must have enough actuators: the controller document maps every actuator it uses to a joint or wheel, and the gateway must provide at least that many.
- Connect one robot controller to a gateway. To drive one manipulator through several gateways, use **+ Gateway link** on its Motion Studio node.

# Running Nodes

Nodes run only when you start them. This page covers starting and stopping nodes, reading their state and logs, and opening the controller UIs.

**Real hardware moves.** Starting a gateway or controller that drives real motors can energize them. Before you start such nodes, make sure the robot's surroundings are clear and someone can reach the emergency stop ([Stop Controls](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/hardware_setup/stop_controls/index.md)).

______________________________________________________________________

## 1. Start and Stop One Node

- Select the node and click **Start node** (or **Stop node**) in the inspector, or
- right-click the node and choose **Start node** / **Stop node**.

Start a robot's nodes in dependency order: **gateway first, then its controller**, then nodes that use the controller (navigation, applications). Stop them in the reverse order.

A controller refuses to start until it has a document and its `servo_link` is connected:

- *Import a robot file (.sdd/.sddm/.sdda) first.*
- *Connect servo_link to a gateway before starting it.*

______________________________________________________________________

## 2. Start All Nodes

The **Start all nodes** button starts every node that is down, in dependency order: gateways → controllers → compounds → applications. Its menu also offers **Stop all nodes**, which stops consumers first. Once every node is up, the button itself reads **Stop all nodes**.

The run menu

- While a run is in progress, a banner shows its progress (*Starting all nodes…* or *Stopping all nodes…*). To cancel, click **Cancel** on the banner, or the button, which reads **Cancel start** or **Cancel stop** during the run. Nodes already started stay up when you cancel.
- The run continues even if you close the browser. The page shows its progress again when you reopen it.
- The result appears as a banner, for example *Runtime topology is up.*

**Start all nodes** starts every node of the graph, including nodes that drive real hardware. When the graph contains hardware you do not want to run, start the nodes one by one.

After Stellar X restarts, the Station comes back with its saved graph, documents and settings, but **no node is started**. Start the nodes again when you need them.

______________________________________________________________________

## 3. Node States

The footer of each node card and the inspector header show the node's state.

| State                      | Meaning                                                                    |
| -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Planned**                | Saved in the graph, not started yet                                        |
| **Booting** / **Starting** | Starting up                                                                |
| **Waiting binding**        | A required port has no connection yet                                      |
