| **Waiting target**         | A connected node is not ready yet                                          |
| **Ready**                  | Started and waiting to operate                                             |
| **Operating**              | Running normally                                                           |
| **Running**                | The process is up                                                          |
| **Paused**                 | Paused                                                                     |
| **Degraded**               | Running with reduced performance                                           |
| **Disconnected**           | Heartbeat lost                                                             |
| **Fault**                  | The node reported a fault. The inspector and the node log show the reason. |
| **Error** / **Failed**     | The node reported an error. The inspector shows the reason.                |
| **Stopped**                | The process ended                                                          |

The dot next to the state is green for Ready, Running and Operating, yellow while waiting, red for errors and grey otherwise. Problems are also counted in the **N issues** chip of the toolbar.

______________________________________________________________________

## 4. Open the Controller UIs

When a node runs, its tools unlock, in the inspector's **CONTROL** section or as a link on the node card:

| Node             | Button                           | Opens                                                                                                                                         |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Motion Studio    | **Stellar Motion Studio**        | [Motion Studio](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/controllers/motion_studio/index.md) for the manipulator                               |
| Strider          | **Strider**                      | [Strider](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/controllers/strider/index.md) for the mobile base                                           |
| Articulation     | **Articulation**                 | [Articulation](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/controllers/articulation/index.md) for joint control                                   |
| Navigator        | **Strider** link on the card     | Strider's Navigation page                                                                                                                     |
| Camera gateway   | **Camera view** link on the card | The camera image                                                                                                                              |
| Actuator gateway | **Test Stellar Gateway**         | The [Test Console](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/gateways/test_console/index.md), which moves single actuators without a controller |

A running Motion Studio node: the CONTROL button is unlocked

Each UI opens in a new browser tab. You can keep several open, one per robot.

**Test Stellar Gateway** is for a gateway that no robot controller uses. Stop the robot controllers first: the Station does not open a test while a Motion Studio node runs, and starting a robot controller (Motion Studio, Strider or Articulation) ends every running test.

______________________________________________________________________

## 5. Logs

The **LOGS** section of the inspector shows the node's recent output. Choose the stream in the drop-down and click **Refresh**:

| Stream                                   | Contents                                                                                           |
| ---------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Gateway events**                       | Gateway status and problems, each with a hint about what to check (gateways and their controllers) |
| **Standard output** / **Standard error** | The program's output                                                                               |
| **Node log**                             | The node's own log file                                                                            |
| **Process log**                          | Start and stop of the process                                                                      |

Gateway events of a simulation gateway

**Tip:** When a node fails, read **Gateway events** of its gateway first. Most start-up problems (no simulator, wrong robot name, no EtherCAT link, drive faults) are reported there with a hint.

______________________________________________________________________

## 6. Troubleshooting

| Symptom                                               | What to check                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A controller stays in **Waiting binding**             | Its `servo_link` (or another required port) is not connected                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| A simulation gateway runs but the robot does not move | The gateway's **Robot name** must equal the articulation prim name in Isaac Sim; Isaac Sim must be playing; the **Sim host** must be the Isaac Sim computer ([Simulation Gateway](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/gateways/simulation/index.md)) |
| An EtherCAT gateway fails to start                    | Cable to the first drive's IN port, drive power, number of drives ([EtherCAT Gateway](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/gateways/ethercat/#6-troubleshooting))                                                                                     |
| *Process stopped during topology startup*             | A node stopped right after **Start all nodes**. Read its logs, fix the cause, then start again                                                                                                                                                           |
| Changes to a document are refused                     | Stop the node first. A gateway document is also refused while the gateway's test is open: click **Stop test** before you stop the gateway ([Test Console](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/gateways/test_console/#change-the-gateway-document)).  |

# Modules

A **module** is a program packaged to run on the Station as a node. The built-in modules (gateways, controllers, navigation) come with Stellar X. You can install your own modules to add robot behaviors, task logic or custom device interfaces; they run next to the built-in ones and use the same interfaces.

This page installs, updates and removes module packages. To build a package yourself, see [Create Custom Modules](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/extend/custom_modules/index.md).

______________________________________________________________________

## 1. The Modules Page

Click **Modules** in the left sidebar. The page lists the built-in modules and the module packages you installed, including modules that no node uses yet.

The Modules page

| No. | Item                  | Description                                                                      |
| --- | --------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | **Add custom module** | Installs a module package from your PC ([Install a Module](#2-install-a-module)) |
| 2   | **TYPE**              | Gateway, Controller, Compound or Application                                     |
| 3   | **USED BY**           | How many nodes of the graph use the module                                       |

The **⋯** menu of a row offers **Module info** and, for your own modules, **Remove module**.

______________________________________________________________________

## 2. Install a Module

1. Click **Add custom module**.
1. Drop the package (`.tar.gz`) or click **Choose file**, then click **Add module**.

Installing a module package

- Uploading a package with the same name replaces the installed version. Nodes that use it keep their connections; stop and start them to run the new version.
- Built-in modules cannot be replaced.

### Add and Start the Module's Node

1. Click **Add node** and choose the type that the module declares: **Gateway**, **Controller**, **Compound** or **Application** (the `role` in its `subsystem.yaml`: `gateway`, `component`, `compound` or `app`). Your module appears in the list with the **CUSTOM** badge. The status module of [Create Custom Modules](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/extend/custom_modules/index.md), for example, is a `component` and appears under **Controller**.
1. Connect its required ports, for example to a Strider's `mobile_base` or a Motion Studio's `manipulator`.
1. Right-click the node and choose **Start node**, or use **Start all nodes**.

If the module has its own web UI, a link with the module's name appears on its node card while it runs. Its logs appear in the inspector's **LOGS** section.

### Remove a Module

Stop and delete the nodes that use the module, then choose **Remove module** in the **⋯** menu of its row.

# Backup and Restore

The whole Station (its node graph, design documents, settings and Station data) can be saved to one **`.sdr`** file and loaded again on the same or another Stellar X. Use it to back up a working system, to copy a system to another robot, or to bring a Station built in Sodero Cloud onto a robot.

An `.sdr` file does not contain installed module packages. To restore a Station on another Stellar X, prepare that unit first ([Load on Another Stellar X](#3-load-on-another-stellar-x)).

______________________________________________________________________

## 1. Export the Station

Click **Export SDR** in the Runtime toolbar. Pending edits are saved first, then the browser downloads a file named after the Station, for example `stellar-x.sdr`.

The file contains:

| Part            | Contents                                                                                         |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Runtime graph   | All nodes and their connections                                                                  |
| Robot documents | The `.sdd`, `.sddm` and `.sdda` documents of the controllers                                     |
| Station data    | Gateway documents (`.gw`), settings of sensor and navigation nodes, maps and other Station state |

Installed module packages are not part of the file; they stay on the controller.

**Tip:** Export the Station before larger changes, such as importing a new document over a working one or loading another `.sdr`.

______________________________________________________________________

## 2. Load an `.sdr` File

1. Stop all nodes (**Start all nodes** menu › **Stop all nodes**).
1. Click **Load SDR**, drop the file or click **Choose file**.
1. Click **Load and restart**.

Loading an .sdr file

The Station replaces its graph, robot documents and Station data with the file's content and restarts. The page shows *Restarting the Station with …* and reloads when the Station is back, usually within a minute. The nodes are not started; start them when you need them.

- Installed modules stay installed.
- If the file cannot be loaded, the Station keeps its data and the dialog says why.
- After a successful load there is no command to return to the previous Station. Export the Station before you load another `.sdr` if you may need it again.

Loading is refused while any node runs: *Stop all nodes before loading a .sdr.*

### Files That Cannot Be Loaded

| Message                                                              | Cause                                                                                                                                                                           |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| *This .sdr holds a simulation, not a Station.*                       | The file is a World (simulation) export. Open it in Sodero Cloud.                                                                                                               |
| *This robot does not have enough free disk space to load this .sdr.* | The unpacked file is too large for the controller's storage.                                                                                                                    |
| *This .sdr uses an obsolete document format (…).*                    | Documents in the file, named in the message, use the format of an earlier Stellar software version. Nothing is loaded. Contact [Sodero support](https://www.sodero.io/contact). |

______________________________________________________________________

## 3. Load on Another Stellar X

An `.sdr` file carries the Station, not the software of the unit. Before you load it on another Stellar X:

1. Make sure that the other unit runs the same version of the Stellar software as the unit the file comes from.
1. Install the module packages that the Station's nodes use, in the same versions, on the other unit's [Modules](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/station/modules/index.md) page. Built-in modules come with the unit.
1. Load the file as described in [Load an `.sdr` File](#2-load-an-sdr-file).
1. Check each node before you start it: the simulator address (**Sim host**) and camera addresses, which belong to the original site, and on real hardware the EtherCAT wiring and the drives, which must match the gateway documents. Start the gateways first and test real hardware as on a new robot.
# Gateways and Sensors

# Gateways Overview

A **gateway** is the node that connects the Station to the physical world: motors, drives and sensors, real or simulated. Controllers never talk to hardware directly. They exchange commands and states with a gateway through a port, and the gateway translates them for the fieldbus or the simulator.

```
flowchart TB
    C["Controllers<br>Motion Studio · Strider · Articulation"] -- servo_link --> AG["Actuator gateway"]
    AG -- "EtherCAT" --> D["EtherCAT drives"]
    AG -- "simulation" --> I["Isaac Sim robot"]
    CG["Camera gateway"] --> N["Visual odometry · Localizer"]
    IG["IMU gateway"] --> L["Legged locomotion · Visual odometry"]
    I -. "camera" .-> CG
    I -. "IMU" .-> IG
```

Because only the gateway knows the hardware, the same controller and controller document can drive a simulated robot and the real one. To move from Isaac Sim to real motors, you give the robot an EtherCAT gateway document. Before you operate the real robot, verify its actuator mapping, calibration, limits and sensor settings: motor directions, gear ratios, encoder resolution and sensor mounting are properties of the hardware.

______________________________________________________________________

## Built-in Gateways

| Module           | Node ID                        | Connects                                                                                                                                                      | Configured with                                                                                                                         |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Actuator gateway | `sodero.actuator_gateway.NAME` | EtherCAT drives, or the joints of a robot in Isaac Sim                                                                                                        | A `.gw` document ([Gateway Designer](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/gateways/gateway_designer/index.md))                       |
| Camera gateway   | `sodero.camera_gateway.NAME`   | An RGB-D camera: a camera in Isaac Sim, or a real camera through the [Device Bridge](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/gateways/device_bridge/index.md) | Camera settings in the inspector ([Cameras and IMUs](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/gateways/sensors_and_cameras/index.md))    |
| IMU gateway      | `sodero.imu_gateway.NAME`      | An IMU (and foot contacts in Isaac Sim): in Isaac Sim, or through the Device Bridge                                                                           | IMU settings in the inspector ([Cameras and IMUs](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/gateways/sensors_and_cameras/#2-imu-gateway)) |

For devices the built-in gateways do not cover, you can write your own gateway as a module with the role `gateway` ([Create Custom Modules](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/extend/custom_modules/index.md)). Once installed, it appears in **Add node** › **Gateway** with the **CUSTOM** badge.

______________________________________________________________________

## Actuator Gateway Types

The `.gw` document chooses how the actuator gateway reaches its actuators:

| Type          | `hardware.type` | Use                                                                                        | Page                                                                                       |
| ------------- | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **EtherCAT**  | `ethercat`      | CiA 402 servo drives on the controller's EtherCAT port, synchronized by distributed clocks | [EtherCAT Gateway](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/gateways/ethercat/index.md)     |
| **Isaac Sim** | `simulation`    | The joints of a robot in NVIDIA Isaac Sim, through the Isaac Bridge extension              | [Simulation Gateway](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/gateways/simulation/index.md) |

______________________________________________________________________

## Actuators and Indices

A gateway drives a list of **actuators**, numbered from zero in the order they are defined (actuator 1 is index 0, actuator 2 is index 1, …). For EtherCAT, the order of the actuators is the order of the drives on the cable.

A controller's document refers to these indices to say which actuator drives which joint or wheel. For example, a Strider document for a 4-wheel base maps its wheels to the gateway's actuators `[0, 1, 2, 3]`.

Motor units and joint units are defined in different documents:

| Unit                            | Where it is defined                                                                           |
| ------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Motor (rpm, Nm, encoder counts) | The gateway's actuator specification: gear ratio, torque and speed limits, encoder resolution |
| Joint or wheel (rad, rad/s, m)  | The controller's document: kinematics, limits, and the mapping from actuators to joints       |

______________________________________________________________________

## Safety Behavior

- **Watchdog.** If a controller stops sending commands while the servo is on, the gateway keeps the last command for 3 s, then switches the servo off.
- **Limits.** The gateway clamps velocity and torque commands to the actuator limits of its document. Position limits come from the controller's document.
- **Emergency stop.** When a controller or the [test console](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/gateways/test_console/index.md) requests an emergency stop, the gateway sends a quick stop to the EtherCAT drives and switches the servo off. How the drives slow down depends on their quick stop settings. These software stops do not replace the hardware emergency stop ([Stop Controls](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/hardware_setup/stop_controls/index.md)).
- **Fault reporting.** Drive faults, lost communication and missing devices are reported in the gateway's **Gateway events** log with a hint about what to check ([Running Nodes](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/station/running_nodes/#5-logs)).
- **One hardware type per gateway.** A gateway drives either real drives on one bus or one simulated robot. Use separate gateways for separate buses.

Next: [Gateway Designer](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/gateways/gateway_designer/index.md), to make the `.gw` document of an actuator gateway.

# Gateway Designer

Every actuator gateway runs from a gateway document (`.gw`): the hardware type, the list of actuators, each actuator's motor and drive parameters, and the fieldbus settings. **Stellar Gateway Designer**, the part of [Stellar Designer](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/tutorials/stellar_designer/introduction/index.md) for `.gw` files, creates and edits these documents. It opens from an actuator gateway node on the Station.

This page covers what all gateway documents share. The settings of each hardware type follow on [Simulation Gateway](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/gateways/simulation/index.md) and [EtherCAT Gateway](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/gateways/ethercat/index.md).

______________________________________________________________________

## 1. Open the Gateway Designer

1. Select an actuator gateway node on the Station.
1. Click **Edit Stellar Gateway Designer** in the **DEFINITION** section.

The Gateway Designer opens in a new tab with the node's document. Edits are saved back to the node automatically. **Stop the gateway before you edit**; the Station refuses saves while it runs (*Gateway '…' is running — stop it in the Station, then save again.*) and while its [test console](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/gateways/test_console/index.md) is open (*Gateway '…' has a test console open — stop the test in the Station, then save again.*).

A simulation gateway with four actuators

| Area              | Contents                                                                                                                                                     |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Breadcrumb        | Where the document belongs: device / Station / node / file. The arrow returns to the Station.                                                                |
| Steps             | **01 Gateway setup** (actuators and their parameters) and **02 Verification**                                                                                |
| **Actuators (N)** | One card per actuator, in index order, with its brand, model and status (**Configured** / **Not configured**). **Add Actuator** adds one; **×** removes one. |
| Actuator panel    | The parameters of the selected actuator, in tabs: **Motor** and a tab for the hardware type (**EtherCAT** or **Isaac Sim**)                                  |
| Units             | `mm / g / deg` or `m / kg / radian` for display                                                                                                              |

______________________________________________________________________

## 2. Choose the Hardware Type

A new gateway node starts with an empty document. When you open it, the Gateway Designer asks for the hardware type:

Create gateway definition

| Type            | Use                                                                                                                                |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Isaac Sim** ① | A robot in NVIDIA Isaac Sim ([Simulation Gateway](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/gateways/simulation/index.md))           |
| **EtherCAT** ②  | CiA 402 servo drives on the EtherCAT port ([EtherCAT Gateway](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/gateways/ethercat/index.md)) |

Select the type and click **Next** ③, then **Create**.

To change the type of an existing gateway, click the Stellar mark at the top left and choose **Definition** › **Replace definition**. Pick the new type and click **Next** › **Replace**. Existing actuators keep their motor settings and receive the new type's hardware settings; the previous type's hardware settings are removed. This cannot be undone.

______________________________________________________________________

## 3. Add and Configure Actuators

1. Click **Add Actuator** once per motor. Actuator 1 is index 0, actuator 2 is index 1, and so on.
1. Select an actuator card. Fill in the **Motor** tab: pick the motor from the catalog (**Brand** › **Series** › **Model**) or enter its values.
1. Fill in the tab of the hardware type: **EtherCAT** (identification, SDOs, PDOs) or **Isaac Sim** (DOF offset).

### Motor Parameters

Every field of the **Motor** tab is described in [EtherCAT Gateway › Motor Tab](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/gateways/ethercat/#motor-tab). For simulation gateways the **Motor** tab shows only **Max torque**, **Max speed** and **Gear ratio**: the gateway limits torque commands to *Max torque × Gear ratio* and velocity commands to *Max speed ÷ Gear ratio* at the joint.

______________________________________________________________________

## 4. Verify and Export

Open **02 Verification** and click **Verify**. The Gateway Designer checks the hardware type, the actuator list, the motor parameters (for EtherCAT also the encoder resolution) and the configuration files.

All checks passed

Errors (for example a parameter that must be positive) must be fixed; warnings are advisory. Then start the gateway from the Station.

When all checks pass, **Export .gw** downloads the document as a `.gw` file, which you can import into another gateway node (**Import .gw**).

______________________________________________________________________

## 5. Simulation Gateways

For **Isaac Sim** gateways, the actuator panel has an **Isaac Sim** tab with one setting:

The Isaac Sim tab of an actuator

**DOF offset** is the first joint of the Isaac Sim articulation that this gateway drives, counted from 0 in actuator order. It applies to every actuator of the gateway: the **Isaac Sim** tab of each actuator shows the same value. Leave it at 0 when one gateway drives the whole robot.

Several gateways can share one simulated robot. For an arm with four joints and a gripper with two, as in the hint below the field (*arm 0, gripper 4*):

| Gateway | DOF offset | Drives     |
| ------- | ---------- | ---------- |
| Arm     | 0          | Joints 1–4 |
| Gripper | 4          | Joints 5–6 |

The robot's name in the scene (**Robot name**) and the address of the Isaac Sim computer (**Sim host**) are set on the Station node, not in the document ([Simulation Gateway](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/gateways/simulation/#2-create-a-simulation-gateway)).

Next: [Simulation Gateway](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/gateways/simulation/index.md) for a robot in Isaac Sim, or [EtherCAT Gateway](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/gateways/ethercat/index.md) for real drives.

# Simulation Gateway

A **simulation gateway** is an actuator gateway of type **Isaac Sim**. Instead of a fieldbus it drives the joints of a robot in NVIDIA Isaac Sim, through the [Isaac Bridge](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/virtual_simulation/extension_installation/index.md) extension on the Isaac Sim computer. The controller connected to it (Motion Studio, Strider, Articulation) uses the same interface as with real motors, so its document and your applications carry over to the real robot. The real robot still needs its own checks: motor directions, gear ratios, encoders, limits and sensors.

```
flowchart TB
    subgraph SX ["Stellar X"]
        C["Controller"] -- servo_link --> G["Simulation gateway<br>Robot name: jackal"]
    end
    subgraph PC ["Isaac Sim computer"]
        B["Isaac Bridge"] --> R["/World/jackal<br>articulation"]
    end
    G -- "commands · TCP 53333" --> B
    B -- "joint states · TCP 53334" --> G
```

______________________________________________________________________

## 1. The Name Rule

**The gateway's Robot name must be exactly the name of the robot's articulation prim in the Isaac Sim scene.**

Isaac Bridge serves every articulation in the scene under the name of its prim: the robot at `/World/jackal` is served as `jackal`. A simulation gateway subscribes to the robot whose name equals its **Robot name**. If the names differ (`Jackal` vs. `jackal`, `jackal_1` vs. `jackal`), the gateway never receives a joint state, keeps waiting and the robot never moves.

| Station (gateway)                 | Isaac Sim (scene)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| --------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Robot name** `jackal`           | Articulation prim `/World/jackal`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Actuator 1, 2, 3, 4 (indices 0–3) | The robot's 1st, 2nd, 3rd and 4th movable joint (revolute or prismatic), in USD order. Joints marked `rc:passive` are skipped ([Prepare the Robot › Joints and Drives](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/virtual_simulation/robot_setup/#4-joints-and-drives)). |
| **DOF offset** 0                  | The gateway starts at the robot's first movable joint ([Gateway Designer › Simulation Gateways](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/gateways/gateway_designer/#5-simulation-gateways))                                                                            |

Use names with lowercase letters, digits and `_`, starting with a letter. Every robot in the scene must have a unique prim name.

______________________________________________________________________

## 2. Create a Simulation Gateway

1. Add an **Actuator gateway** node on the Station.

1. Either import a simulation `.gw` (**Import .gw**), or click **Edit Stellar Gateway Designer**, choose **Isaac Sim**, and add one actuator per joint of the robot ([Gateway Designer](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/gateways/gateway_designer/index.md)).

1. In the node's **TARGET** section, click **Change** and set:

   - **Robot name** ①: the articulation prim name (see the rule above).
   - **Sim host** ②: the IP address of the Isaac Sim computer.

   Click **Done** ③. Changes take effect when the gateway starts next time.

① Robot name ② Sim host ③ Done

### Addresses Set for the Controller

Sodero can set two addresses for a controller on request: a **simulator address** and a **camera address**. They point to the Isaac Sim computer, or to the [Device Bridge](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/gateways/device_bridge/index.md) computer for real sensors. When an address is set, the gateways use it at every start:

| Address           | Used by                                                                                                                                                                |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Simulator address | Simulation gateways, in place of **Sim host**. The IMU gateway, which has no address field, connects only to this address; without it, the IMU gateway does not start. |
| Camera address    | Camera gateways, in place of **Camera host**. The **Camera host** field is then greyed out and shows this address.                                                     |

Each gateway's log shows the address it uses, for example *Simulation: robot 'jackal', simulator at 192.168.60.20; waiting for it to start.* ([Check the Connection](#3-check-the-connection)). To have an address set or changed for your controller, contact Sodero.

______________________________________________________________________

## 3. Check the Connection

Start Isaac Sim's scene (**Play**), then start the gateway. Its **Gateway events** log shows:

```
Simulation: robot 'jackal', simulator at 192.168.60.20; waiting for it to start.
Simulator connected.
```

| Log message                                                 | Meaning                                                                                     |
| ----------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| *waiting for it to start*                                   | No joint state arrives yet. Normal until Isaac Sim plays. If it stays, see Troubleshooting. |
| *Simulator connected.*                                      | Joint states arrive; the controller can switch the servo on.                                |
| *Simulator connection lost; servo turned OFF.*              | The simulation stopped or the network dropped. The gateway reconnects by itself.            |
| *Simulator connected again; turn the servo on to continue.* | Switch the servo on again in the controller UI.                                             |

When the simulation is stopped and played again, Isaac Sim puts the robot back at its starting pose, and the controller's servo is off until you switch it on again.

______________________________________________________________________

## 4. Several Robots and Shared Robots

- **Several robots:** add one gateway (and controller) per robot, each with its own **Robot name**. All of them use the same Isaac Sim computer and ports.
- **One robot, several gateways:** an arm and its gripper can be driven by two gateways on the same articulation, each with its own **DOF offset** ([Gateway Designer › Simulation Gateways](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/gateways/gateway_designer/#5-simulation-gateways)).

______________________________________________________________________

## 5. Troubleshooting

| Symptom                                                | Cause and fix                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| The log stays at *waiting for it to start*             | Isaac Sim is not playing; the address in the log line is not the Isaac Sim computer (**Sim host**, or the [simulator address](#addresses-set-for-the-controller) set for the controller); its firewall blocks TCP 53333–53334; **Robot name** does not match the prim name                                                                 |
| The Isaac Bridge window does not list the robot        | The prim has no PhysX articulation root, or another robot in the scene has the same prim name ([Prepare the Robot › Check the Robot](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/virtual_simulation/robot_setup/#9-check-the-robot))                                                                                                           |
| The Isaac Bridge window shows the robot as *not bound* | The robot is not a valid PhysX articulation. Check the Isaac Sim console ([Prepare the Robot › Check the Robot](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/virtual_simulation/robot_setup/#9-check-the-robot)).                                                                                                                               |
| Servo on is accepted but the robot does not move       | Strider: the drive mode is not **Twist**. Motion Studio: the joint count of the scene differs from the gateway's actuators.                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| A wheel or joint turns the wrong way                   | The joint order or axis in the scene differs from the document. Fix the scene or the document; do not invert signs elsewhere.                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Motion looks slow, or localization lags                | The simulation runs slower than real time: controllers follow simulation time, but camera-based localization runs on wall-clock time. Lower the scene's physics and render rates, close other GPU programs ([Real-Time Performance](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/virtual_simulation/connect_station/#6-real-time-performance)). |

# EtherCAT Gateway

Stellar X is an EtherCAT master. An actuator gateway of type **EtherCAT** drives CiA 402 servo drives on the controller's EtherCAT port with distributed-clock synchronization at the gateway's control period (1 ms by default). This page covers wiring, the gateway document, parameters, bring-up and troubleshooting.

For a complete example from wiring to driving, see [EtherCAT Mobile Base](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/tutorials/ethercat_mobile_base/index.md): four drives on a skid-steer base, with example files.

**Real motors move.** Bring up a new EtherCAT system with the robot clear of people and obstacles, the drives' safe torque off (STO) and emergency stop wired, and someone at the emergency stop ([Stop Controls](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/hardware_setup/stop_controls/index.md)).

______________________________________________________________________

## 1. What You Need

| Item       | Requirement                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Drives     | EtherCAT servo drives with the CiA 402 profile, supporting cyclic synchronous position (CSP). Mobile bases also need cyclic synchronous velocity (CSV); torque control needs cyclic synchronous torque (CST). |
| Drive data | The drive's ESI file (EtherCAT Slave Information, `.xml`) from the manufacturer, unless the drive is in the built-in catalog                                                                                  |
| Motor data | Rated and peak torque, maximum speed, encoder resolution, gear ratio                                                                                                                                          |
| Cables     | Standard EtherCAT (Ethernet) cables, one per drive                                                                                                                                                            |

Built-in catalog: **Panasonic MINAS A6BE**, **RS Automation CSD7**, **MyActuator RMD-X (EtherCAT)** drives, and Panasonic MSMD, RS Automation CSMA/CSMT and MyActuator RMD-X motors.

______________________________________________________________________

## 2. Wire the Drives

Connect the drives as a line, starting at Stellar X:

```
flowchart LR
    SX["Stellar X"] --> D1["Drive 1"]
    D1 --> D2["Drive 2"]
    D2 --> D3["Drive 3"]
```

- Plug Stellar X's **EtherCAT Out** port into the **IN** port of the first drive. Connect each drive's **OUT** port to the next drive's **IN** port.
- **Do not use a network switch.** EtherCAT frames must pass through the drives in a line.
- **The cable order is the actuator order.** The first drive on the cable is actuator 1 (index 0) of the gateway, the second is actuator 2 (index 1), and so on. To change the order, change the wiring.
- Devices after the last controlled drive are allowed; the gateway ignores them.
- The EtherCAT port needs no IP address and is not configured on the Network Settings page.

______________________________________________________________________

## 3. Create the Gateway Document

1. On the Station, add an **Actuator gateway** node, for example `arm` ([Nodes and Connections](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/station/nodes_and_connections/index.md)).
1. Click **Edit Stellar Gateway Designer**. In **Create gateway definition**, choose **EtherCAT** and click **Next** › **Create** ([Gateway Designer](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/gateways/gateway_designer/index.md)).
1. Click **Add Actuator** once per drive, in cable order.
1. For each actuator, fill in the **Motor** tab and the **EtherCAT** tab as described below.
1. Open **02 Verification**, click **Verify** and fix any errors.

An EtherCAT gateway with two actuators; the EtherCAT tab of actuator 1

### Motor Tab

Motor tab

Click **Brand**, **Series** or **Model** ① to open **Motor Select**: search by model number, or pick **Brand** › **Series** › **Model**. The preview shows the catalog values, and **Accept** fills them in. For a motor that is not in the catalog, type the values.

Motor Select catalog: search ①, or pick Brand ② › Series ③ › Model ④, then Accept ⑤

The fields of the **Motor** tab (simulation gateways show only **Max torque**, **Max speed** and **Gear ratio**):

| Section                 | Field              | Unit  | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ----------------------- | ------------------ | ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| ② TORQUE                | **Rated torque**   | Nm    | Continuous motor torque. Torque commands are sent to the drive in per mille of this value.                                                                                                                 |
|                         | **Max torque**     | Nm    | Peak torque of the motor itself, at the motor shaft (the motor's datasheet value, not the torque after the reducer). The gateway limits torque commands to *Max torque × Gear ratio* at the joint.         |
| ③ SPEED                 | **Max speed**      | rpm   | Maximum speed of the motor itself, at the motor shaft (the motor's datasheet value, not the joint speed after the reducer). The gateway limits velocity commands to *Max speed ÷ Gear ratio* at the joint. |
| ④ MOTOR CHARACTERISTICS | **Resolution**     | PPR   | Encoder pulses (counts) per motor revolution, **before** the gear, e.g. 1,048,576 (2²⁰) or 8,388,608 (2²³)                                                                                                 |
| ⑤ ENCODER CONFIGURATION | **Encoder offset** | pulse | Zero offset of the absolute encoder. Origin calibration (**Set origin** in Motion Studio) sets it; leave 0 for a new robot and do not enter it by hand.                                                    |
| ⑥ REDUCER               | **Gear ratio**     | ratio | Reduction between motor and joint: motor turns per joint turn                                                                                                                                              |

**Rated torque**, **Max torque** and **Max speed** are the motor's own values at the motor shaft, as in the motor's datasheet, whatever reducer follows it. Do not convert them to the joint side: the gateway applies the **Gear ratio** itself.

If **Gear ratio** is exactly 1, the gateway reads the gear ratio configured in the drive itself (object 0x6091). Enter the real ratio when the drive does not hold it.

### EtherCAT Tab

Click the gear icon in the actuator panel to open **Servo Driver Select**:

Search ① or pick Brand ③ › Series ④ › Model ⑤, or import the drive's ESI file ②. Accept ⑥ fills in the EtherCAT tab.

- Pick the drive from the catalog, or click **ESI Import** ② and choose the drive's ESI `.xml`. If the file describes several devices, choose yours; then choose the RxPDO and TxPDO areas to use.
- **Accept** fills in the drive's identification, start-up SDOs and PDO mapping. Values you change later are highlighted; click one to return to the catalog value.

IDENTIFICATION ①, SDOS ②, PDOS ③

| Section            | Field                                        | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **IDENTIFICATION** | **Idx**                                      | Position of the drive on the cable, from 0 (read-only)                                                                                                                                                                                           |
|                    | **Alias**                                    | An alias that identifies the device (read-only). The gateway addresses drives by their position on the cable, not by alias.                                                                                                                      |
|                    | **Name**                                     | A label for logs                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| **SDOS**           | **Index**, **Subindex**, **Value**, **Size** | Start-up parameters written to the drive before operation. Index, subindex and value are hexadecimal (`0x…`); size is in bytes. The entry named *Absolute Encoder Reset* is not written at start-up; Motion Studio's origin calibration uses it. |
| **PDOS**           | **Rx PDO** / **Tx PDO** index                | The PDO mapping objects, typically `0x1600` and `0x1A00`                                                                                                                                                                                         |
|                    | Entries                                      | The objects exchanged every cycle (see below). **Init Value** sets a constant for extra RxPDO entries.                                                                                                                                           |

**Absolute Encoder Reset needs the drive's own object.** In the built-in catalog, the *Absolute Encoder Reset* entry of some drives, such as the MINAS A6BE, has the index `0x0000`, a placeholder. Before you use origin calibration (**Set origin** in Motion Studio), enter the drive's encoder reset object from its manual: index, subindex, value and size. Keep the entry's name: the gateway finds the entry by it.

### Process Data

The gateway uses these CiA 402 objects:

| Direction          | Object | Name                       | Required                                |
| ------------------ | ------ | -------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| RxPDO (to drive)   | 0x6040 | Controlword                | Yes                                     |
|                    | 0x607A | Target position            | For position control                    |
|                    | 0x60FF | Target velocity            | For velocity control (**mobile bases**) |
|                    | 0x6071 | Target torque              | For torque control                      |
|                    | 0x60B2 | Torque offset              | Optional (feed-forward)                 |
|                    | 0x6060 | Modes of operation         | Optional: carries the mode every cycle  |
| TxPDO (from drive) | 0x6041 | Statusword                 | Yes                                     |
|                    | 0x6064 | Position actual value      | Yes                                     |
|                    | 0x606C | Velocity actual value      | Recommended                             |
|                    | 0x6077 | Torque actual value        | Recommended                             |
|                    | 0x6061 | Modes of operation display | Recommended                             |
|                    | 0x603F | Error code                 | Recommended (fault messages)            |

The gateway writes the mode of operation (0x6060) to each drive itself, by SDO after the drive reaches SAFE-OP, and every cycle when 0x6060 is in the RxPDO. A 0x6060 entry under **SDOS** is ignored.

When a controller drives the gateway, you do not choose the mode of operation: the controller selects it per command. Position commands use CSP (8), velocity commands CSV (9), torque and impedance commands CST (10). In the [test console](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/gateways/test_console/index.md) you choose the drive mode yourself.

### Verify

Open **02 Verification** and click **Verify**. Open a check marked **Error** to see which actuator and which value to fix, then click **Verify again**.

Verification found missing motor parameters and encoder resolution

A Strider (mobile base) drives its wheels in velocity mode. If the drive's RxPDO has no **Target velocity (0x60FF)**, the wheels do not move and the gateway reports it. Choose a PDO mapping that includes 0x60FF.

______________________________________________________________________

## 4. Connect a Controller

1. Add the controller node (Motion Studio, Strider or Articulation) and import its document. The document must name this gateway and its actuator indices ([Design Documents](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/station/design_documents/#5-rules-for-documents)).
1. Connect the controller's `servo_link` to the gateway's `servo_link`.

______________________________________________________________________

## 5. Bring Up the System

1. Power the drives. Release the emergency stop and STO.

1. Select the gateway and click **Start node**. Watch **LOGS** › **Gateway events**:

   ```
   EtherCAT: starting on network port 'eth0' (2 drive(s) expected).
   EtherCAT: found drive 1 (MINAS-A6B).
   EtherCAT: found drive 2 (MINAS-A6B).
   EtherCAT ready: 2 drive(s) operational, 1.0 ms cycle.
   ```

1. Optional: before you start a controller, click **Test Stellar Gateway** in the gateway's **CONTROL** section to open the [test console](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/gateways/test_console/index.md) and move single actuators. When the test is done, click **Servo OFF** in the console and **Stop test** in the gateway's **CONTROL** section. [EtherCAT Mobile Base › Step 5](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/tutorials/ethercat_mobile_base/#step-5-test-the-wheels-with-the-test-console) shows a complete test of four wheels.

1. Start the controller node, open its UI and switch **Servo On**. Jog slowly first and check each joint's direction.

**Tip:** Bring up one drive first. When it reaches *EtherCAT ready* and moves correctly, add the next drive to the cable and to the document.

______________________________________________________________________

## 6. Troubleshooting

The gateway explains every problem in **Gateway events**, followed by a hint. The most common messages:

| Message                                                                         | Cause and fix                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| *EtherCAT: no cable link on network port …*                                     | No Ethernet link. Plug the cable into Stellar X's **EtherCAT Out** port and into the first drive's **IN** port, and power the drive.                                                                                                       |
| *EtherCAT: no drive answered on network port …*                                 | The cable goes to the wrong port of the drive (OUT instead of IN), to a switch, or the drive has no power.                                                                                                                                 |
| *EtherCAT: found M of the N drives this gateway controls.*                      | The chain ends after drive M. Check the cable from drive M's OUT port to the next drive's IN port, and that drive's power.                                                                                                                 |
| *…configuration describes K drive(s), but the gateway controls N.*              | The drive list in the document does not match the actuators. Fix it in the Gateway Designer.                                                                                                                                               |
| *Drive … exchanges x/y bits of process data …, the project describes …*         | The PDO mapping in the document does not match the drive. Re-select the drive or re-import its ESI file.                                                                                                                                   |
| *Drive … did not reach SAFE-OP / OP …*                                          | The drive refused the configuration or the synchronization. The AL status in the message names the reason (sync, watchdog, PDO or cycle time).                                                                                             |
| *Drive … gets velocity commands, but Target Velocity (0x60FF) is not in its …*  | Add 0x60FF to the RxPDO (see [Process Data](#process-data)).                                                                                                                                                                               |
| *Servo ON failed: drive … did not enable (it stays in 'switch on disabled').*   | The drive refuses to switch on: check its STO and enable inputs, the emergency stop and its main power.                                                                                                                                    |
| *Drive … fault: … (error code 0x….)*                                            | A drive alarm, such as overcurrent, voltage, temperature, encoder or following error. Read the alarm on the drive and look it up in its manual, then **Error Reset** / **Fault Reset** in the controller UI and switch the servo on again. |
| *EtherCAT communication lost: the drives stopped answering.*                    | A cable was unplugged or a drive lost power. The message names the segment; fix it and restart the gateway.                                                                                                                                |
| *No commands from the robot controller for 3.0 s: servo turned OFF for safety.* | The controller stopped or lost its connection. Until the 3 s pass, the gateway keeps the last command. Start the controller and switch the servo on again.                                                                                 |

Problems that are not in the gateway's log (such as a joint moving in the wrong direction or the wrong distance) come from the documents: check the actuator order (cable order), **Gear ratio**, **Resolution**, and the joint mapping in the controller's document.

# Test Console

The test console moves the actuators of one actuator gateway without a robot controller. You switch the servo on and off, choose a drive mode, and send position, velocity or torque targets to each actuator. Use it to check the wiring, the directions, the gear ratios and the encoder settings of a gateway before a controller drives the robot. [EtherCAT Mobile Base › Step 5](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/tutorials/ethercat_mobile_base/#step-5-test-the-wheels-with-the-test-console) shows a complete test of four wheels in velocity mode.

**Real motors move.** Test one actuator at a time, with small values, with the mechanism free to move and the hardware emergency stop within reach. The console does not limit position targets, and its **EMERGENCY STOP** does not replace the hardware emergency stop ([Stop Controls](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/hardware_setup/stop_controls/index.md)).

______________________________________________________________________

## Open the Test Console

The test console is for a gateway that no robot controller uses.

1. Stop the robot controllers on the Station. While a Motion Studio node runs, the Station does not open a test and reports that a robot controller is running. Starting a robot controller (Motion Studio, Strider or Articulation) ends every running test.
1. Select the gateway and click **Start node**. **Test Stellar Gateway** in its **CONTROL** section unlocks when the gateway runs.
1. Click **Test Stellar Gateway**. The console opens in a new browser tab.
1. If the console shows **Gateway not connected**, click **Connect**. The console always connects with the servo off.

While the test runs, the console is a node of the graph, `sodero.actuator_test.NAME` (`NAME` is the gateway's name), connected to the gateway's `servo_link`. It has a red dashed outline because it is not part of your saved graph; do not add it with **Adopt running**. The gateway's **CONTROL** section shows **Open test console**, which opens the console again, and **Stop test**.

① the test console, connected to the gateway's servo_link ② the gateway's test console buttons

______________________________________________________________________

## Screen Layout

① EMERGENCY STOP ② Servo ON and Servo OFF ③ the drive mode of all actuators ④ the target velocity of actuator 1

| Area                                 | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Top bar                              | The gateway, and the connection: **Gateway Connected**, **Gateway Disconnected**, **connecting…** or **Starting…**. The theme menu and the **deg** / **rad** button change the display only.                                                            |
| **SERVER LOG**                       | Messages of the console's own connection to the gateway. The gateway's events, such as drive faults and *Servo ON: all N drive(s) enabled.*, are in the gateway's **LOGS** › **Gateway events** on the Station page.                                    |
| **EMERGENCY STOP** ①                 | Quick stop of every drive of the gateway, with the servo off. Click it again to release it, then click **Servo ON**.                                                                                                                                    |
| **SERVO CMD** ②                      | **Servo ON** and **Servo OFF** for all actuators of the gateway; **Fault Reset** resets drive faults. After a fault reset, switch the servo off and on again.                                                                                           |
| **DRIVE MODE — APPLY TO ALL AXES** ③ | The drive mode of every actuator: **POSITION**, **VELOCITY**, **TORQUE** or **IMPEDANCE**. **Apply** sets it, sets every position target to the measured position and every velocity and torque target to zero.                                         |
| **Trajectory ON**                    | On: a new position target is approached smoothly, in about 1 to 2 s. Off: the target is sent as a step.                                                                                                                                                 |
| Actuator cards **A1**, **A2**, …     | One card per actuator, in the gateway's order (**A1** is actuator 1, index 0): its own **Drive Mode** menu, the servo indicator **Enable** / **Disable**, the target sliders and the measured values **Actual qa**, **Actual dqa** and **Actual taua**. |

Targets and measured values are at the joint, after the gear: degrees (or radians), degrees per second and newton-meters.

______________________________________________________________________

## Drive Modes

| Mode          | Command                                                                                                                       | When the actuator moves                                                                                         |
| ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **POSITION**  | **qa_d · Target Position**, ±180°                                                                                             | When you release the slider, the actuator moves to the new position.                                            |
| **VELOCITY**  | **dqa_d · Target Velocity**, ±180 °/s                                                                                         | While you hold the slider. On release the target returns to 0.                                                  |
| **TORQUE**    | **taua_d · Torque Feedforward**, ±10 Nm                                                                                       | While you hold the slider. On release the target returns to 0.                                                  |
| **IMPEDANCE** | **qa_d · Target Position**, with the stiffness **K** (Nm/rad, 10 by default) and the damping **D** (Nm·s/rad, 0.5 by default) | The actuator is pulled toward the target position like a spring with a damper. Enter K and D, then press Enter. |

Only the slider of the actuator's drive mode commands it. The gateway limits velocity and torque commands to the limits of its document; position targets are not limited, so keep them inside the range the mechanism can move. In TORQUE mode nothing limits the speed: use small torques.

When a controller drives the gateway, it chooses the drive mode itself for each command. In the test console you choose it ([EtherCAT Gateway › Process Data](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/gateways/ethercat/#process-data)).

______________________________________________________________________

## Run a Test

1. Choose the drive mode under **DRIVE MODE — APPLY TO ALL AXES** and click **Apply**.
1. Click **Servo ON**. Check the gateway's log on the Station page for *Servo ON: all N drive(s) enabled.* The cards show **Enable** as soon as the gateway accepts the request, so only the log line confirms that every drive is enabled.
1. Move one actuator with a small value, and check its direction and travel against the measured value.
1. When you are done, click **Servo OFF**.

______________________________________________________________________

## End the Test

1. Click **Servo OFF** in the console.
1. Click **Stop test** in the gateway's **CONTROL** section. The test node leaves the graph.

Closing the console's tab does not end the test.

The console keeps sending the last command until you change it. If its tab closes or the network drops while an actuator moves, the actuator keeps moving. Open the console again with **Open test console** and click **Servo OFF** or **EMERGENCY STOP**, or press the hardware emergency stop. **Stop test** without **Servo OFF** leaves the last command active for up to 3 s, until the gateway's watchdog switches the servo off.

______________________________________________________________________

## Change the Gateway Document

The Station refuses to save a gateway document while the gateway runs and while its test is open. To change a value found in a test, for example a drive's polarity:

1. Click **Servo OFF** in the console.
1. Click **Stop test** in the gateway's **CONTROL** section.
1. Click **Stop node** on the gateway.
1. Change the document in the [Gateway Designer](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/gateways/gateway_designer/index.md), or import a new `.gw`.
1. Click **Start node** on the gateway, then **Test Stellar Gateway**, and test again.

Stop the test before you stop the gateway. While the gateway is stopped, its **CONTROL** section shows no **Stop test**, and saves stay refused (*Gateway '…' has a test console open*). In that case, start the gateway again, click **Stop test**, and then stop the gateway.

______________________________________________________________________

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom                                                                                                                              | Cause and fix                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| The Station refuses to open the test because a robot controller is running, or the console shows **A controller is already running** | A Motion Studio node runs. Stop it, then click **Connect** in the console.                                                                 |
| The console shows **Gateway not connected**                                                                                          | Click **Connect**. If it does not connect, check that the gateway is **Operating**.                                                        |
| The cards show **Enable**, but the gateway's log shows *Servo ON failed*                                                             | A drive did not enable. Check its STO and enable inputs, the emergency stop and its main power, then click **Servo OFF** and **Servo ON**. |
| An actuator does not react to a slider                                                                                               | The slider does not belong to the actuator's drive mode, or the servo is off.                                                              |
| After **EMERGENCY STOP** is released, a drive does not enable again                                                                  | Click **Servo ON**. If the drive still does not enable, click **Stop test**, stop and start the gateway, and open the test again.          |
| The test ended by itself                                                                                                             | A robot controller was started on the Station.                                                                                             |

# Cameras and IMUs

Stellar Station has built-in gateways for the two sensors its navigation and walking controllers use: an **RGB-D camera** and an **IMU**. In simulation they read the cameras and IMUs of Isaac Sim. For real sensors, a small computer next to the sensors runs the [Device Bridge](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/gateways/device_bridge/index.md), which serves real devices exactly as Isaac Sim serves simulated ones.

```
flowchart TB
    I["Isaac Sim + Isaac Bridge<br>(simulation)"]
    DB["Device Bridge<br>(real camera / IMU)"]
    I -- "TCP 53335" --> CG["Camera gateway"]
    DB -- "TCP 53335" --> CG
    I -- "TCP 53334" --> IG["IMU gateway"]
    DB -- "TCP 53334" --> IG
    CG --> VO["Visual odometry"]
    CG --> LOC["Localizer"]
    IG --> VO
    IG --> LEG["Legged locomotion"]
```

| Your sensor                                                    | Use                                                                                                                                                      |
| -------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A camera or IMU in Isaac Sim                                   | Camera gateway / IMU gateway, connected to Isaac Sim (this page)                                                                                         |
| A real RGB-D camera (e.g. Intel RealSense) or USB IMU          | The [Device Bridge](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/gateways/device_bridge/index.md) on a sensor computer, plus the Camera gateway / IMU gateway |
| Any other device (digital I/O, force sensors, custom hardware) | Your own gateway module ([Create Custom Modules](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/extend/custom_modules/index.md))                                |

______________________________________________________________________

## 1. Camera Gateway

Add the node with **Add node** › **Gateway** › **Camera gateway** and a name such as `cam0`. Nodes that use the camera connect to its `camera` port.

The camera gateway's inspector

### Connection

In the **CAMERA GATEWAY** section of the inspector:

| Field           | Value                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| --------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Camera name** | The name of the camera: in Isaac Sim, the camera prim's name (for example `cam0` for `/World/jackal/links/base_link/cam0`); with the Device Bridge, the bridge's robot name                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| **Camera host** | The address of the Isaac Sim computer or the sensor computer. When a camera address is set for the controller, the field is greyed out and the gateway uses that address at every start, even if an uploaded YAML names another ([Addresses Set for the Controller](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/gateways/simulation/#addresses-set-for-the-controller)). |
| **Port**        | `53335`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |

### Camera Settings

Stop the camera node to enable its settings, change the values, click **Save settings**, then start it again. If navigation is already running, cancel its active goal and stop Navigator, Localizer and the camera in that order; restart the camera, Localizer and Navigator after saving ([full procedure](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/navigation/simulation_tutorial/#correct-settings-on-a-running-setup)).

Default field of view is 60°

A new camera gateway starts with **horizontal fov deg = 60**, **fps = 15** and **width = height = 0** (automatic size detection). Match the field of view to the source camera before using localization. For the [Jackal warehouse tutorial](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/navigation/simulation_tutorial/#step-2-add-the-camera-gateway), change the field of view to **90** and fps to **5**, keeping width and height at **0**. A different camera needs its own calibration; do not apply 90° to every camera.

| Setting               | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **fps**               | Expected frame rate (the source decides the actual rate)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **frame id**          | Name of the camera's optical frame, at most 15 characters, for example `cam0_optical`. The map bundle's extrinsics refer to this name.                                                                                                                                                                     |
| **width**, **height** | Image size; 0 takes it from the frames                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Intrinsics            | `fov` mode with the horizontal field of view in degrees, or `manual` mode with fx, fy, cx, cy in pixels. A new camera gateway offers only the field of view; load `manual` values with **Upload yaml** ([Device Bridge › Camera](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/gateways/device_bridge/#camera)). |
| Simulation camera     | Connection timeouts                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |

Isaac Sim renders cameras with square pixels and the principal point at the image center, so `fov` mode with the camera's horizontal field of view is exact. Isaac Bridge prints each camera's field of view in the Isaac Sim console when the scene plays.

### See the Image

While the camera gateway runs, click **Camera view** on its node card:

Camera view of cam0: frame rate, frame age and resolution

______________________________________________________________________

## 2. IMU Gateway

Add the node with **Add node** › **Gateway** › **IMU gateway**. Nodes that use the IMU connect to its ports.

| Setting                    | Meaning                                                                                                 |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Robot in World**         | The robot whose IMU to read: its articulation prim name in Isaac Sim, or the Device Bridge's robot name |
| **Sample rate (Hz)**       | IMU sample rate (default 250)                                                                           |
| **Sensor event rate (Hz)** | Rate of the published IMU events (default 20)                                                           |

The IMU gateway has no address field: it connects to the simulator address set for the controller, which must be the Isaac Sim computer or the sensor computer of the Device Bridge ([Addresses Set for the Controller](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/gateways/simulation/#addresses-set-for-the-controller)).

In Isaac Sim, a robot publishes IMU data when its robot prim names the link that carries the IMU in `rc:imuLink` ([Prepare the Robot › IMU](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/virtual_simulation/robot_setup/#7-imu)).

______________________________________________________________________

## 3. Mounting: Where the Sensor Sits

Sensor data is in the sensor's own frame. Where the camera is mounted on the robot (its position and orientation relative to the robot's `base_link`) is part of the map bundle's extrinsics, used by the Localizer ([Load and Configure a Map](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/navigation/map_bundle/#3-check-the-values-for-the-first-run)). Measure the mounting on the robot; do not rotate the data in the source.
