**Tip:** The [Quick Start](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/get_started/quick_start/index.md) uses a prepared Jackal scene and its example files. Do step 1 first; the Quick Start then covers steps 2 and 3 for the Jackal.

# Install Isaac Bridge

**Isaac Bridge** is the Isaac Sim extension that connects Isaac Sim to the gateways of Stellar Station. Install it once on the computer that runs Isaac Sim.

______________________________________________________________________

## 1. Download the Extension

The source of Isaac Bridge is published on GitHub. Download release **v1.0.0**, the version this documentation is verified with ([Compatibility](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/reference/compatibility/index.md)):

```
git clone --branch v1.0.0 https://github.com/Sodero-labs/isaac_bridge.git
```

Or download the source ZIP file of release v1.0.0 from the repository's **Releases** page, extract it, and rename the extracted folder `isaac_bridge-1.0.0` to `isaac_bridge`. Either way you get a folder `isaac_bridge`. Remember the folder that **contains** it, for example `~/isaac_extensions` when the extension is in `~/isaac_extensions/isaac_bridge`.

______________________________________________________________________

## 2. Add the Extension to Isaac Sim

1. Start Isaac Sim.
1. Open **Window › Extensions**.
1. Open the Extensions window's settings (the menu icon next to the search field) and add the folder that contains `isaac_bridge` to **Extension Search Paths**.
1. Search for `isaac bridge` ①.
1. Switch the extension on ②.
1. Tick **AUTOLOAD** ③, so the extension starts with Isaac Sim from now on.

① search ② enable ③ autoload

When the extension starts the first time, Isaac Sim installs the Python package `pyzmq` from the internet. For a computer without internet access, download the package on a computer that has internet access and the same operating system and Isaac Sim version, copy the `wheels` folder to the Isaac Sim computer, and install it from there. Run the commands in Isaac Sim's installation folder:

```
# On the computer with internet access
./python.sh -m pip download pyzmq -d wheels
# On the Isaac Sim computer, with the copied wheels folder
./python.sh -m pip install --no-index --find-links wheels pyzmq
```

```
REM On the computer with internet access
python.bat -m pip download pyzmq -d wheels
REM On the Isaac Sim computer, with the copied wheels folder
python.bat -m pip install --no-index --find-links wheels pyzmq
```

You can also start Isaac Sim with the extension from a command line: `isaac-sim.sh --ext-folder ~/isaac_extensions --enable isaac_bridge` (`isaac-sim.bat` on Windows).

______________________________________________________________________

## 3. Open the Status Window

Open **Window › Isaac Bridge**. The window shows what the bridge serves. Before a scene plays it is mostly empty; press **Play** in Isaac Sim and it fills in:

The Isaac Bridge status window while a scene plays

| No. | Line        | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                |
| --- | ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | **Ports**   | The command (53333), state (53334) and camera (53335) ports, and **serving** when the gateways can connect. The line below shows the scene's physics and render rates. |
| 2   | **Robots**  | Every robot of the scene: its name, its prim path, **bound** when the bridge controls it, and its number of joints (DOF)                                               |
| 3   | **Cameras** | Every camera served: name, resolution, frame rate and frames sent                                                                                                      |
| 4   | **Rescan**  | Looks for robots and cameras again after you changed the scene while it plays                                                                                          |

The command and state ports (53333, 53334) open at the first **Play** and stay open until the scene is closed. The camera port (53335) opens at each **Play** when the scene has cameras, and closes at **Stop**.

______________________________________________________________________

## 4. Allow the Ports in the Firewall

Stellar X connects to the Isaac Sim computer on **TCP ports 53333, 53334 and 53335**. Allow them for incoming connections from Stellar X.

```
sudo ufw allow from <Stellar X IP address> to any port 53333:53335 proto tcp
```

Open **Windows Defender Firewall › Advanced settings › Inbound Rules › New Rule…**, choose **Port**, **TCP**, ports `53333-53335`, and allow the connection for your private network.

The bridge does not authenticate its clients: any computer that reaches these ports can command the robots of the scene. Use it on a trusted network only, and do not open the ports to the internet.

______________________________________________________________________

## 5. Update or Remove

- **Update:** put the new release into the same `isaac_bridge` folder: run `git fetch --tags` and `git checkout RELEASE_TAG` in the folder (a clone of a release tag cannot `git pull`), or replace the folder with the new release's ZIP as in [step 1](#1-download-the-extension). Restart Isaac Sim and check the connection again: the [status window](#3-open-the-status-window) shows the ports **serving** and your robots **bound**, and each simulation gateway logs *Simulator connected.* Check [Compatibility](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/reference/compatibility/index.md) for the versions this documentation is verified with.
- **Remove:** switch the extension off in **Window › Extensions**, untick **AUTOLOAD**, and remove its folder from **Extension Search Paths**.

The extension's [README](https://github.com/Sodero-labs/isaac_bridge/blob/v1.0.0/docs/README.md) describes advanced settings, such as camera sizes and rates, which cameras to publish, and the ports.

Next: [Prepare the Robot](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/virtual_simulation/robot_setup/index.md).

# Prepare the Robot

Isaac Bridge serves every robot of the open scene that follows a few rules. This page explains them and how to prepare your own robot. Worlds exported from Sodero Cloud already follow them, and so does the example scene of the [Quick Start](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/get_started/quick_start/index.md) (`jackal_warehouse.usd`): open it to see a working example.

______________________________________________________________________

## 1. The Rules

| Rule                                                                                                                                           | Why                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **The robot is a PhysX articulation.** Its top prim carries an **Articulation Root** with the PhysX articulation API (`PhysxArticulationAPI`). | The bridge finds robots by the attribute `physxArticulation:articulationEnabled` of that API. A prim with only the USD Physics articulation root (`UsdPhysics.ArticulationRootAPI`) is not found. |
| **The prim name is the robot name.** It is unique in the scene and equal to the **Robot name** of the robot's gateway on the Station.          | Gateways address robots by this name.                                                                                                                                                             |
| **The joints, in their USD order, are the actuators.**                                                                                         | Actuator 1 of the gateway is the robot's first movable joint, actuator 2 the second, and so on.                                                                                                   |
| **Links are under `links`, joints under `joints`.**                                                                                            | Sensors refer to links by their name under `links`.                                                                                                                                               |
| **Z up, meters.**                                                                                                                              | Joint values are exchanged in radians (revolute joints) and meters (prismatic joints).                                                                                                            |

A robot prepared this way looks like this in the **Stage** panel:

① the robot prim jackal with the Articulation Root ② its four drive joints in actuator order

```
/World/jackal              ← Articulation Root; prim name = robot name
    links/
        base_link          ← rigid body (with cameras below it)
        wheel_fl, wheel_fr, wheel_rl, wheel_rr
    joints/
        drive_fl           ← actuator 1
        drive_fr           ← actuator 2
        drive_rl           ← actuator 3
        drive_rr           ← actuator 4
```

______________________________________________________________________

## 2. Start from a Model

- **Isaac Sim assets.** Isaac Sim ships many robots from well-known manufacturers. Find them in the **Isaac Sim Assets** browser (**Window › Browsers**).
- **URDF.** Import a URDF with Isaac Sim's URDF importer (**File › Import**). See [Import URDF](https://docs.isaacsim.omniverse.nvidia.com/latest/importer_exporter/import_urdf.html) in the Isaac Sim documentation.
- **A 3D model.** Rig the robot yourself: rigid bodies and colliders on the links, joints between them, and an articulation root. See [Articulate a Basic Robot](https://docs.isaacsim.omniverse.nvidia.com/latest/robot_setup_tutorials/tutorial_gui_simple_robot.html) in the Isaac Sim documentation.

Then check the model against the rules above; the sections below show how to fix what differs.

______________________________________________________________________

## 3. Articulation Root and Name

1. Select the robot's top prim in the **Stage** panel, for example `/World/jackal`.
1. Right-click it and choose **Add › Physics › Articulation Root**. A robot has exactly one articulation root; remove any other articulation root inside the robot.
1. Rename the prim to the robot name. Use lowercase letters, digits and `_`, and start with a letter.

The robot name must be unique in the scene. If two robots share a name, the bridge serves only the later one in the scene, lists only that one, and warns in the Isaac Sim console: *two devices are named '…' (… and …); only … is served*.

**Fixed-base robots** (manipulators) are fixed to the world by a **Fixed Joint** from the world to their base link. Create it inside the robot (select the base link, **Create › Physics › Joint › Fixed Joint**) and leave **Body 0** empty, which means the world. Mobile and walking robots have no such joint.

______________________________________________________________________

## 4. Joints and Drives

**Joint order.** Actuator *i* of the gateway is the *i*-th revolute or prismatic joint under the robot prim, in the order the joints are stored in the USD file. The **Stage** panel shows this order when it is sorted **Old to New** (the default). Fixed joints do not count.

| Gateway              | Isaac Sim         |
| -------------------- | ----------------- |
| Actuator 1 (index 0) | 1st movable joint |
| Actuator 2 (index 1) | 2nd movable joint |
| …                    | …                 |

When the order of the scene differs from the order your controller document expects, change the actuator mapping in the document, or re-create the joints in the order you need.

**Drives.** Give every actuated joint a drive: right-click the joint and choose **Add › Physics › Angular Drive** (revolute) or **Linear Drive** (prismatic). The bridge sets the drive gains for each command mode. Set the drive's **Max Force** to the joint's real torque or force limit.

**Limits and zero.** The joint's lower and upper limits and its zero position come from the USD joint. Make the zero position match the zero of the real robot, so that the same document works for both.

**Starting pose.** Each time the scene plays, the robot starts where it was authored: its root at its position in the scene and every joint at its authored joint state, or at zero. Velocities start at zero.

**Passive joints.** Joints that are not actuators, such as caster wheels, are marked with the attribute `rc:passive = true` on the joint; they then do not count in the actuator order.

______________________________________________________________________

## 5. Physics and Mass

- Every link is a rigid body with a collider and a realistic mass. Wrong masses make torques, hand guiding and walking unrealistic.
- Wheels need friction: give the floor and the wheels a physics material with realistic friction.
- The bridge runs physics at the rate authored on the scene's **PhysicsScene** prim (`rc:physicsHz`) and renders at `rc:renderHz`. Without them it uses 60 Hz for both. Use at least 120 Hz physics for mobile robots and higher rates for walking robots; a lower render rate (20–30 Hz) leaves more time for physics. The render rate is lowered automatically so that each rendered frame runs a whole number of physics steps.

The current rates appear in the [Isaac Bridge status window](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/virtual_simulation/extension_installation/#3-open-the-status-window).

______________________________________________________________________

## 6. Cameras

Every **Camera** prim of the scene (except Isaac Sim's own viewport cameras) is served under its prim name, with color and depth images (640 × 480 at 15 frames per second by default). Cameras render only while the scene plays.

The camera cam0 under the Jackal's base_link

1. Create a camera under the link it is mounted on (**Create › Camera**), for example `/World/jackal/links/base_link/cam0`, so it moves with the robot.
1. Place and point it as on the real robot.
1. Give it a unique name. The Station's camera gateway uses this name as **Camera name**.
1. Note its horizontal field of view: the camera gateway needs it ([Cameras and IMUs](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/gateways/sensors_and_cameras/index.md)). Isaac Bridge prints each camera's field of view in the Isaac Sim console when the scene plays.

To change a camera's size or frame rate, or to publish only some cameras, follow **Cameras** in the extension's [README](https://github.com/Sodero-labs/isaac_bridge/blob/v1.0.0/docs/README.md#cameras).

______________________________________________________________________

## 7. IMU

Walking robots need an IMU, and visual odometry can use one. The bridge emulates an IMU on a link of the robot when the robot prim carries these attributes:

| Attribute (on the robot prim) | Type   | Meaning                                                                      |
| ----------------------------- | ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `rc:imuLink`                  | string | Name of the link under `links` that carries the IMU, for example `base_link` |
| `rc:imuOffset`                | float3 | Position of the IMU in that link's frame, in meters (default 0, 0, 0)        |

The Station's IMU gateway then reads it under the robot name ([Cameras and IMUs](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/gateways/sensors_and_cameras/#2-imu-gateway)). It connects to the simulator address set for the controller ([Addresses Set for the Controller](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/gateways/simulation/#addresses-set-for-the-controller)).

______________________________________________________________________

## 8. Add Attributes with the Script Editor

Attributes such as `rc:physicsHz`, `rc:imuLink` or `rc:passive` are custom USD attributes. Add them with **Window › Script Editor**, then save the scene (**File › Save**):

```
import omni.usd
from pxr import Gf, Sdf

stage = omni.usd.get_context().get_stage()

# physics and render rates of the scene
scene = stage.GetPrimAtPath("/World/PhysicsScene")
scene.CreateAttribute("rc:physicsHz", Sdf.ValueTypeNames.Float).Set(120.0)
scene.CreateAttribute("rc:renderHz", Sdf.ValueTypeNames.Float).Set(30.0)

# an IMU on the base link of my_robot, 5 cm above the link origin
robot = stage.GetPrimAtPath("/World/my_robot")
robot.CreateAttribute("rc:imuLink", Sdf.ValueTypeNames.String).Set("base_link")
robot.CreateAttribute("rc:imuOffset", Sdf.ValueTypeNames.Float3).Set(Gf.Vec3f(0.0, 0.0, 0.05))

# a caster that is not an actuator
caster = stage.GetPrimAtPath("/World/my_robot/joints/caster_joint")
caster.CreateAttribute("rc:passive", Sdf.ValueTypeNames.Bool).Set(True)
```

Replace the prim paths with those of your scene.

______________________________________________________________________

## 9. Check the Robot

Press **Play** and open **Window › Isaac Bridge**:

| What you see                            | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| --------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `my_robot /World/my_robot bound, 6 DOF` | Ready. The DOF count must equal the number of actuators of the robot's gateway(s).                                                                                                                                                       |
| The robot is not listed                 | The prim has no PhysX articulation root (`physxArticulation:articulationEnabled`), or another robot in the scene has the same prim name: the bridge serves only the later one and warns in the Isaac Sim console (*… only … is served*). |
| The robot is listed but not bound       | It is not a valid PhysX articulation (check the Isaac Sim console).                                                                                                                                                                      |
| The DOF count is too high               | Passive joints are not marked with `rc:passive`.                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| A camera is missing                     | Two cameras share a name, or the camera is one of Isaac Sim's viewport cameras.                                                                                                                                                          |

Next: [Connect to Stellar Station](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/virtual_simulation/connect_station/index.md).

# Connect to Stellar Station

With Isaac Bridge installed and the robot prepared, point the Station's gateways at Isaac Sim and drive the robot.

______________________________________________________________________

## 1. Play the Scene

1. Open the scene in Isaac Sim and press **Play**.
1. Open **Window › Isaac Bridge** and check that the ports are **serving** and your robot is **bound**.

① ports serving ② robots bound ③ cameras served ④ Rescan

______________________________________________________________________

## 2. Set the Gateways on the Station

Set the Station nodes to match Isaac Sim. For a simulation gateway, select it, click **Change** in its **TARGET** section, enter **Robot name** ① and **Sim host** ②, and click **Done** ③. The values apply when the gateway starts next time.

| Isaac Sim                    | Station node                  | Field                                                                              |
| ---------------------------- | ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Robot `jackal`               | Actuator gateway (simulation) | **TARGET › Robot name** `jackal`                                                   |
| The Isaac Sim computer       | Actuator gateway (simulation) | **TARGET › Sim host**: the computer's IP address                                   |
| Camera `cam0`                | Camera gateway                | **Camera name** `cam0`, **Camera host**: the computer's IP address, **Port** 53335 |
| Robot `jackal` (with an IMU) | IMU gateway                   | **Robot in World** `jackal`                                                        |

The IMU gateway has no address field: it connects to the simulator address set for the controller, which must be the Isaac Sim computer. When a simulator address is set, it also replaces **Sim host** at every start of a simulation gateway. The gateway's log shows the address in use ([Addresses Set for the Controller](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/gateways/simulation/#addresses-set-for-the-controller)).

**The Robot name on the Station must be exactly the robot's prim name in Isaac Sim.** Names are case-sensitive. If they differ, the gateway keeps waiting and the robot never moves.

The TARGET section of a simulation gateway: ① Robot name ② Sim host ③ Done

How to create the gateways and their documents: [Simulation Gateway](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/gateways/simulation/index.md), [Cameras and IMUs](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/gateways/sensors_and_cameras/index.md).

______________________________________________________________________

## 3. Start and Drive

1. Start the gateways, then the controllers ([Running Nodes](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/station/running_nodes/index.md)).
1. Each simulation gateway logs *Simulator connected.*
1. Open the controller's UI, switch the servo on, and jog: [Strider](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/controllers/strider/index.md) for mobile bases, [Motion Studio](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/controllers/motion_studio/index.md) for manipulators.

The Jackal jogged from Strider

______________________________________________________________________

## 4. Stop, Pause and Play

The gateways treat Isaac Sim like a power supply of real drives:

| In Isaac Sim                            | Result                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| --------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Pause**                               | The robots stay where they are. The gateways see the simulator stop and switch the servo off; switch it on again after you resume.                                                                                                                                                  |
| **Stop**, then **Play**                 | A new session: the robots start again at their authored pose, as after a power cycle. Switch the servo on again.                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Editing the scene while it plays        | Takes effect at the next **Play**, or click **Rescan** in the Isaac Bridge window                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Closing Isaac Sim and starting it again | The gateways lose the simulator and switch the servo off, and the controllers stop the robots. The gateways reconnect by themselves: when the scene plays again, wait until the gateway logs *Simulator connected again; turn the servo on to continue.*, then switch the servo on. |

After the simulation restarts, the robot is back at its starting pose, but the Localizer may still hold its last pose. If Strider's Navigation page shows a wrong pose, set the initial pose again.

______________________________________________________________________

## 5. Several Robots

One scene can hold several robots. Add one gateway (and controller) per robot on the Station, each with its own **Robot name**. All gateways use the same Isaac Sim computer and ports; the status window lists every robot it serves.

A robot can also be driven by several gateways, for example an arm and its gripper. Each gateway drives its own range of joints, set by its **DOF offset** ([Gateway Designer](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/gateways/gateway_designer/#5-simulation-gateways)).

______________________________________________________________________

## 6. Real-Time Performance

The simulation runs in real time while the computer keeps up with the render rate. The controllers follow the simulation's time, but camera-based localization runs on wall-clock time, so a simulation that runs slower than real time degrades localization.

- Use moderate camera sizes and frame rates; each camera is rendered in addition to the viewport.
- Close viewports and windows you do not need.
- Do not run other heavy GPU programs (such as training) on the same computer at the same time.
- Keep the clocks of both computers synchronized (NTP). The camera gateway accepts frames at most 20 ms ahead of and 2 s behind its own clock. If you cannot synchronize them, start Isaac Sim with `RC_CAMERA_CAPTURE_TIME=0`: the camera gateway then stamps each frame when it arrives.

______________________________________________________________________

## 7. Troubleshooting

| Symptom                                                                                       | Cause and fix                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The status window does not show **serving**                                                   | Another program (for example a second Isaac Sim) holds ports 53333–53335. Close it and press **Play** again.                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Gateway log stays at *waiting for it to start*                                                | Isaac Sim is not playing, **Sim host** (or the simulator address set for the controller) is not the Isaac Sim computer, or a firewall blocks the ports ([Install Isaac Bridge](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/virtual_simulation/extension_installation/#4-allow-the-ports-in-the-firewall)) |
| Isaac Sim console: *'sim_command' for 'X', which is no robot or tracked object of this stage* | The gateway's **Robot name** `X` is not the prim name of a robot in the scene                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| The Isaac Bridge window does not list the robot                                               | The prim has no PhysX articulation root, or another robot in the scene has the same prim name ([Prepare the Robot](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/virtual_simulation/robot_setup/#9-check-the-robot))                                                                                        |
| The robot is listed but never **bound**                                                       | It is not a valid PhysX articulation (check the Isaac Sim console)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Camera gateway: *publishes frames of camera(s) … but none of camera …*                        | The camera gateway's **Camera name** is not the camera's prim name                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Camera gateway: frames *stale* or with capture times that do not match                        | The clocks of the two computers differ. Synchronize them, or start Isaac Sim with `RC_CAMERA_CAPTURE_TIME=0` so that the camera gateway uses arrival times.                                                                                                                                           |
| The robot moves too fast or too slow                                                          | The computer cannot keep up with the render rate. Lower camera sizes or rates, or close viewports.                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

The Isaac Sim console shows the bridge's messages, prefixed with the robot or camera name.
# Operate Robots

# Strider

**Stellar Strider** controls wheeled mobile bases. A Strider node (`sodero.mlc.NAME`) turns body velocities into wheel commands for its gateway, integrates odometry, and enforces the speed and acceleration limits of its `.sddm` document. The Strider web UI lets you jog the base, watch its state and odometry, and send navigation goals.

Supported drive types (templates of the `.sddm` document): differential drive, skid steer 4WD, mecanum 4WD, swerve 4WD and Ackermann.

______________________________________________________________________

## 1. Open Strider

On the Station, start the gateway first, then the Strider node ([Running Nodes](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/station/running_nodes/index.md)). Click **Strider** in the node's **CONTROL** section, or the **Strider** link on the node card. Strider opens in a new tab for that robot.

A running Strider node

Each Strider tab controls one robot. With several mobile robots, open one tab per robot from its own node. The **Strider** link on a Navigator node opens Strider directly on its Navigation page.

______________________________________________________________________

## 2. Screen Layout

The left rail has three pages: **Status**, **Drive** and **Navigation**. The top bar shows the readiness pill, **System Log**, **Motion Alarm**, **E-STOP** and the units on every page, plus the actions of the current page: **Jog** on Status, **Stop Motion** on Drive, **Set Goal** and **Start Navigation** on Navigation.

| Item                         | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Readiness pill               | The current state in one line, for example *Manual Drive Ready* or *Servo Off*. Click it for the **CHECKS** list: Connection, Mobile base, Servo, Localization, Navigation.                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **System Log**               | Events of this browser session, with filters for System, Drive, Navigation and Localization                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **Motion Alarm**             | Active alarms and recent errors                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **Stop Motion** (Drive page) | Stops manual driving and cancels a running goal                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **E-STOP**                   | Software stop of the base: cancels driving and the navigation goal and sets the wheel speeds to zero at once, with the servo still on. It latches until **Clear E-Stop**, which switches the base to **Idle**. It does not replace the hardware emergency stop ([Stop Controls](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/hardware_setup/stop_controls/index.md)). |
| Units                        | `m / m/s / deg` or `m / m/s / rad`. Display only; commands are always SI.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |

The readiness checks

______________________________________________________________________

## 3. Status Page

The Status page

| Card                           | Contents                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Trajectory (Odometry View)** | The path driven since the last mode change, in the odometry frame. Buttons recenter, zoom, go full screen and clear the trail. |
| **Operation Status**           | System Ready, Moving / Motion Idle, Servo On / Off, Fault Clear / Emergency Stop / Fault / Watchdog Tripped                    |
| **Base Status (Odometry)**     | Mode and X, Y, Theta, VX, VY, WZ                                                                                               |
| **Control Node Health**        | Whether the base, the localizer and the navigator are reachable                                                                |
| **Drive Unit Status**          | The drive template (for example `skid_steer_4`) and, per wheel, the servo state, position, velocity and target velocity        |
| **Recent Events**              | The six latest events; **View All** opens the **System Log**                                                                   |

**Watchdog Tripped** while the base stands still in Twist mode is normal: it means that no velocity command is arriving, so the base holds zero speed.

______________________________________________________________________

## 4. Jog the Base (Drive Page)

The Drive page

### Step by Step

1. Make sure the area around the robot is clear and you can reach the emergency stop.
1. Under **Drive Mode**, click **Twist** ①.
1. Under **Servo / Safety**, switch **Servo On** ②. The readiness pill shows *Manual Drive Ready*.
1. Set the speed limits ④: **Linear Velocity Limit** (default 0.2 m/s, at most 0.8 m/s) and **Angular Velocity Limit**.
1. Press and hold a pad button ⑤: **Forward (W)**, **Backward (S)**, **Turn Left (A)**, **Turn Right (D)**. The base moves only while you hold the button and stops when you release it; **Stop (Space)** stops it too. The base slows down at the acceleration limits of its document.
1. To drive with the keyboard, switch on **Live** ③ in **Manual Drive**, then use **W**, **S**, **A**, **D** and **Space**.
1. When you are done, switch the servo off and click **Idle**.

| No. | Control            | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| --- | ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | **Drive Mode**     | **Idle**: no motion; the wheels stop at once. **Twist**: body velocity commands (jogging and navigation). **Wheel**: direct wheel speeds (advanced). **EMG**: stops the base like **E-STOP**, but does not latch. |
| 2   | **Servo On / Off** | Enables or disables the drives. **Fault Reset** clears drive faults; afterwards switch the servo off and on again. **Clear E-Stop** releases a latched **E-STOP**.                                                |
| 3   | **Live**           | Sends commands at 20 Hz from the keyboard. Commands stop when the window loses focus.                                                                                                                             |
| 4   | Velocity limits    | Upper limits for manual driving                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| 5   | Drive pad          | Hold-to-drive buttons                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| 6   | **Stop Motion**    | Stops manual driving and any navigation goal                                                                                                                                                                      |
| 7   | **E-STOP**         | Software stop that latches ([Stop Controls](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/hardware_setup/stop_controls/index.md))                                                                                       |
| 8   | Readiness pill     | Why driving is or is not possible right now                                                                                                                                                                       |

Manual commands take priority over navigation: jogging during a navigation goal overrides the navigator and can end the goal. Every manual command expires after about a second, so manual driving stops by itself if the connection drops. A navigation goal does not: cancel it with **Stop Motion**, **Cancel** or **E-STOP**.

### Advanced Controls

Click **Show** next to **Advanced Controls** for:

| Section             | Use                                                                                                                             |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Wheel Direct**    | Command each wheel's speed (Wheel mode)                                                                                         |
| **Preview Command** | See which wheel speeds a body velocity would produce, without moving (safe with the servo off)                                  |
| **Steering Origin** | Set the zero angle of steered wheels                                                                                            |
| **Calibration**     | Differential drive: reset odometry and calibrate wheel radius and track width by driving 1 m straight and turning half a circle |
| **Record / Replay** | Record a manual drive for a number of seconds and replay it                                                                     |

______________________________________________________________________

## 5. Navigation Page

The Navigation page appears when a Localizer and a Navigator run on the Station ([Localization and Navigation](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/navigation/overview/index.md)).

The Navigation page after a goal was reached

| Card                                     | Contents                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ---------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Navigation Map (Occupancy Grid)**      | The map of the loaded map bundle, the robot, the planned path and the goal. Layers: Trajectory, Global Path, Local Path, Obstacles, Robot Footprint. Drag to pan, scroll to zoom. |
| **Mission Status**                       | Running, Idle or Paused                                                                                                                                                           |
| **Current Pose (Map)** / **Goal Pose**   | Where the robot is on the map and where it is going                                                                                                                               |
| **Localization Status**                  | Healthy, Degraded, Initializing, Relocalizing, Lost or Uninitialized, with position quality and ICP error. **Global localization** searches the whole map when the robot is lost. |
| **Route Summary**                        | Distance remaining, estimated time of arrival                                                                                                                                     |
| **Navigator**                            | Navigator state, the base connection and a **Speed Limit** slider (10–100 %)                                                                                                      |
| **Navigation Controls**                  | **Set Initial Pose**, **Set Goal**, **Clear Goal**, **Pause**, **Resume**, **Cancel**                                                                                             |
| **Recent Goals** / **Navigation Events** | Goals sent from this browser and their results; navigation events                                                                                                                 |

### Set the Initial Pose

If the localization status is not **Healthy**, tell the localizer where the robot is:

1. Click **Set Initial Pose** ①.
1. Press on the map where the robot stands and drag in the direction it faces ②.
1. Click **Set initial pose** (or **Relocalize here** ③ when a pose was set before).

Setting the initial pose on the map

### Send a Goal

1. Make sure the base is in **Twist** with the servo on (the readiness pill shows *Navigation Ready*).
1. Click **Set Goal**, press on the map where the robot should go and drag in the direction it should face.
1. Click **Start Navigation**. The planned path appears, and **Navigator** shows *following*.

Following the path to a goal

**Pause** cancels the goal and keeps it; **Resume** sends it again. **Cancel** stops navigation.

______________________________________________________________________

## 6. Control Strider from Programs

The main functions are also available to programs:

- From the SSH workspace with `sodero tools call strider.set_mode`, `strider.servo_on`, `strider.set_twist`, `strider.stop` and `strider.get_state` ([sodero CLI](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/ssh_workspace/sodero_cli/index.md)).
- From your own modules on the Station through the `mobile_base` interface ([Create Custom Modules](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/extend/custom_modules/index.md)).

```
sodero tools call strider.get_state --input '{"target": "sodero.mlc.jackal"}'
sodero tools call strider.set_mode --input '{"mode": "TWIST", "target": "sodero.mlc.jackal"}' --execute
```

`strider.set_twist` is a single velocity sample that expires after a short time. A program that drives continuously must send samples several times per second, and must stop the robot with `strider.stop` when it ends.

# Motion Studio

**Stellar Motion Studio** is the controller UI for manipulators. A Motion Studio node (`sodero.mmc.NAME`) runs the arm's real-time controller: kinematics, dynamics, trajectory generation and safety limits from the arm's `.sdd` document. The Motion Studio web UI lets you watch the arm in 3D, jog it, define tools and teach poses.

______________________________________________________________________

## 1. Open Motion Studio

1. On the Station, add a **Motion Studio** node and an **Actuator gateway**, load the `.sdd` and `.gw` documents and connect `servo_link` ([Nodes and Connections](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/station/nodes_and_connections/index.md)).
1. Start the gateway, then the Motion Studio node.
1. Click **Stellar Motion Studio** in the node's **CONTROL** section. Motion Studio opens in a new tab for that arm.

______________________________________________________________________

## 2. Screen Layout

The Home page

| No. | Item                   | Description                                                                                 |
| --- | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | Pages                  | **Home**, **Tool** and **Pose**                                                             |
| 2   | 3D view                | The arm in its current pose, with its 3D model from the `.sdd`                              |
| 3   | **Joint Status**       | Per joint: position, target position, velocity, target velocity, effort and residual effort |
| 4   | **TCP Status**         | Position and orientation of the tool center point, and its linear and angular velocity      |
| 5   | **Active Tool Status** | The active tool's TCP offset, center of mass and payload mass                               |
| 6   | **Filters**            | Shows or hides the cards of the Home page                                                   |

### Header

The header

| No. | Item                  | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| --- | --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| 1   | Robot and role        | The controller node and whether this window has control (*Pilot - Control Active*)                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| 2   | **Manual** / **Auto** | **Manual** limits the linear speed of the tool center point in the controller's own motions and jogs, 0.25 m/s by default. It is a software limit for teaching, not a safety-rated reduced speed, and it does not limit rotations or **Hand** mode. **Auto** runs at the programmed speed. |
| 3   | Feed rate             | Speed override in percent (10–150 %), applied to motion in progress                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| 4   | **Error Reset**       | Clears a protective stop (a joint at its limit, a speed or torque limit, a detected collision) and resets drive faults. Switch the servo on again afterwards. If the arm stays stopped, stop and start the Motion Studio node.                                                             |
| 5   | Units                 | `mm / g / deg` or `m / kg / radian`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| 6   | **Jog**               | Opens the jog panel                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| 7   | **Command log**       | Commands sent from this window                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| 8   | **Alarm**             | Active alarms and notifications                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

The Stellar mark at the top left opens the menu: **Back to Stellar Station**, **File** (import and export tools and poses), **Set origin**, **Help & Feedback** and **About Stellar Motion Studio**.

The menu

______________________________________________________________________

## 3. Jog the Arm

Click **Jog** in the header to open the jog panel.

The jog panel

1. Switch **Servo On** ⑥.
1. In **JOG OPTION** ②, choose the jog **Mode** ③:
   - **Joint**: move one joint at a time (J1…Jn).
   - **Base**: move the tool in the robot's base frame (X, Y, Z, RX, RY, RZ).
   - **Tool**: move the tool in its own frame.
   - **Hand**: hand guiding. The arm compensates gravity so you can move it by hand; the jog buttons are disabled. There is no damping and no speed limit, and collision detection stays active, so a firm push can cause a protective stop.
1. Choose **Continuous** (moves while you hold a button) or **Step** (5° or 10 mm per click) ④, and the **Speed** ⑤ (50 %, 100 % or 150 %, about 0.04, 0.1 and 0.2 m/s at the tool).
1. Hold **−** or **+** next to a joint or axis in **JOG CONTROL** ⑦. Motion stops when you release the button.

The **POSE** section ① shows the current TCP pose and joint positions.

**Keep the hardware emergency stop within reach.** Motion Studio has no on-screen emergency stop ([Stop Controls](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/hardware_setup/stop_controls/index.md)). A continuous jog moves until the page receives the release of the button: if the browser or the connection fails while you hold it, the motion continues. Do not leave the window while jogging, and make sure the payload is set correctly before you use **Hand** mode.

______________________________________________________________________

## 4. Tools

The **Tool** page defines the tools mounted on the flange.

The Tool page

1. Click **+** ① to add a tool and rename it with the pencil icon (for example `gripper`).
1. Enter the **TOOL CENTER POINT** ③: the TCP position and orientation relative to the flange. The calculator icon ④ opens **TCP Calibration**, which computes the TCP from 3–10 poses that touch the same point.
1. Enter the **PAYLOAD PROPERTIES** ⑤: center of mass, inertia and mass. The calculator icon ⑥ opens **Payload Calibration**.
1. Click **Save** ⑦, or **Save and Apply** ⑧ to make it the active tool at once. **Set as active tool** ② activates a saved tool.

A wrong payload makes hand guiding and collision detection unreliable. Set the mass and center of mass of every tool you mount.

______________________________________________________________________

## 5. Poses

The **Pose** page stores named poses.

The Pose page

1. Jog the arm to the pose, then click the camera icon ① (**Save Current Pose**). Or click **+** ② (**Add pose**) and fill in the values.
1. Select the pose in the list ③. **POSE DATA** shows its TCP pose and joint positions; the icon ④ (**Set from current**) copies the current pose into it.
1. **TEST MOVE** ⑤ moves the arm to the pose: choose **Joint** or **Linear** motion and hold **Hold to move** ⑥. The arm moves only while you hold the button.
1. Click **Save** ⑦.

Saved poses appear as markers in the 3D view. Right-click a pose to copy it, duplicate it or delete it. Use **File** in the menu to export or import tools and poses.

______________________________________________________________________

## 6. Set the Origin

When an absolute encoder is replaced or the arm is reassembled, set the joint origins: menu › **Set origin**, choose the joint, enter its true angle and click **Calibration**. The servo stays off afterwards.

______________________________________________________________________

## 7. Program the Arm

Motion Studio is for setup and teaching. Programs run outside the UI and call the same controller:

| From                    | How                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The SSH workspace       | `sodero tools call motion.move_j`, `motion.move_l`, `motion.get_tcp_pose` and the other `motion.*` tools ([sodero CLI](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/ssh_workspace/sodero_cli/index.md)) |
| A module on the Station | A module node connected to the Motion Studio node's `manipulator` port ([Create Custom Modules](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/extend/custom_modules/index.md))                           |

```
sodero tools call motion.get_tcp_pose --input '{"target": "sodero.mmc.arm"}'
sodero tools call motion.move_j --input '{"target": "sodero.mmc.arm",
  "waypoints": [{"q": {"values": [0, 0, 1.5708, 0, 1.5708, 0]}, "vel": 0.5, "acc": 1.0}]}' --execute
```

Tools use SI units: radians, meters and seconds. Check a tool's arguments with `sodero tools describe motion.move_j` before you call it.

# Articulation

The **Articulation** controller drives an articulated robot joint by joint: legged robots, humanoids, grippers, pan-tilt heads, or any set of joints that receives joint targets. Unlike Motion Studio, it uses no arm kinematics (no DH parameters, no Cartesian motions). It bounds and forwards joint targets from an upper controller, such as the [**Legged locomotion**](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/station/nodes_and_connections/#node-types-and-modules) node that runs a walking policy, and it lets you jog and calibrate the joints by hand.

| Item     | Value                                                                                                                  |
| -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Node     | `sodero.amc.NAME`                                                                                                      |
| Document | `.sdda` ([Stellar Designer](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/tutorials/stellar_designer/articulation/index.md)) |
| Joints   | 1 to 64, driven by one actuator gateway                                                                                |
| Units    | rad, rad/s, N·m                                                                                                        |

```
flowchart TB
    IMU["IMU gateway"] -- imu --> LL["Legged locomotion<br>walking policy"]
    LL -- "joint targets" --> AC["Articulation"]
    AC -- servo_link --> GW["Actuator gateway"]
```

______________________________________________________________________

## 1. The Document

An `.sdda` document lists the joints and how the gateway's actuators drive them.

| Per joint          | Meaning                                                    |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| Name               | Joint name                                                 |
| Position min / max | Range of motion; targets outside it are refused            |
| Velocity max       | Velocity limit; also the reference for the jog speed       |
| Torque max         | Torque limit; the controller clamps its total output to it |
| Offset (optional)  | Joint position at actuator position zero                   |
| Kp, Kd (optional)  | Stiffness and damping, for PD torque control               |

**Drive mode.** In `position` mode the controller bounds the joint targets and the drive (or the simulated joint) follows them with its own position control. In `pd_torque` mode the controller computes a PD torque from Kp and Kd and sends torque commands.

**Actuator mapping.** As for manipulators, influence factors connect actuators to joints; one actuator can move several joints and several actuators can move one joint, as long as the mapping is invertible.

**Watchdogs.** The controller switches the servo off and latches a stop when the gateway's feedback is older than 100 ms or when no new target arrives for 200 ms (the defaults). Click **Clear stop**, then **Servo on**. Reconnecting never switches the servo on by itself.

______________________________________________________________________

## 2. Open the Articulation UI

Start the gateway and the Articulation node, then click **Articulation** in the node's **CONTROL** section.

| Area              | Contents                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Left rail         | **Joints** (joint monitor), **Constraints** (configured limits), **Set origin**                                                                                                                                 |
| Top bar           | **Servo on**, **Servo off**, **Stop** (switches the servo off and latches a stop), **Clear stop** (releases it while the servo is off), the control mode, and the button that opens the **Joint control** panel |
| Status strip      | **Servo** On/Off, **Feedback** age in milliseconds, **Safety** (*Ready* or the reason for a stop)                                                                                                               |
| **Controller**    | The Articulation node this window controls                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **Joint monitor** | Per joint: position, velocity, effort and target                                                                                                                                                                |

**Stop the upper controller first.** Pause or stop Legged locomotion (or any program that sends joint targets) before you jog or calibrate by hand.

______________________________________________________________________

## 3. Jog Joints

1. Open the **Joint control** panel (button at the right of the top bar).
1. Click **Servo on**.
1. Under **Joint jog**, set the **Speed** (1–100 % of each joint's velocity limit; 10 % by default).
1. Hold **−** or **+** next to a joint. The joint moves while you hold the button and holds its position when you release it. A jog button also switches the servo on if it is off.

Leaving the window, switching to another tab or losing the connection switches the servo off.

______________________________________________________________________

## 4. Send Joint Targets

Under **Joint targets**:

1. Click **Use measured positions** to copy the current positions into the target fields.
1. Change the targets of the joints you want to move.
1. Click **Stream targets**. The controller follows the targets while the stream runs; **Stop target stream** ends it and switches the servo off.

______________________________________________________________________

## 5. Set the Origin

**Set origin** assigns an angle to the current position of a joint, for example after an encoder was replaced:

1. Bring the joint to a known position.
1. Choose the joint, then click **Reset current angle to 0**, or enter the true angle (deg or rad) and click **Set current angle**.

The servo switches off first; the joint does not move. Afterwards the servo stays off and a stop is latched: check the joint monitor, click **Clear stop**, then **Servo on**.

Some devices only support setting the origin to zero, and robots in simulation do not support it.

______________________________________________________________________

## 6. Control from Programs

| From                    | How                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ----------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A walking robot         | The **Legged locomotion** node runs a walking policy and sends joint targets to this node                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| The SSH workspace       | `sodero tools call articulation.get_status`, `articulation.get_joint_state`, `articulation.servo_on`, `articulation.uc_pos`, `articulation.stop` ([sodero CLI](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/ssh_workspace/sodero_cli/index.md)); `sodero articulations get` shows the joints and actuators |
| A module on the Station | A module node connected to the Articulation node ([Create Custom Modules](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/extend/custom_modules/index.md))                                                                                                                                                    |
# Localization and Navigation

# Localization and Navigation

Stellar Station includes a complete navigation stack for mobile robots: it knows where the robot is on a map (**localization**) and drives it to goals around obstacles (**navigation**). Both run on Stellar X as built-in nodes and work with the base's Strider node: the localizer reads its odometry, and the navigator drives the base through it.

**Tip:** Start with [Navigate in Simulation](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/navigation/simulation_tutorial/index.md). It sets up the whole stack on the simulated Jackal of the Quick Start, with a finished map, before you make the map of your own site.

______________________________________________________________________

## 1. How It Works

```
flowchart TB
    CAM["Camera gateway<br>RGB-D"] -- camera --> LOC["Localizer<br>sodero.localizer"]
    STR["Strider<br>sodero.mlc.NAME"] -- odometry --> LOC
    LOC -- "localization · map" --> NAV["Navigator<br>sodero.navigator"]
    NAV -- mobile_base --> STR
    MAP[(".nav map bundle")] -.-> LOC
    MAP -.-> NAV
    STR -- servo_link --> GW["Actuator gateway"]
```

| Node                           | Role                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Camera gateway**             | Delivers depth and color images from the robot's RGB-D camera                                                                                                                                                     |
| **Strider**                    | Drives the base and reports **odometry**: how far the wheels have moved the robot                                                                                                                                 |
| **Localizer**                  | Matches the camera's 3D view against the map's point cloud and corrects the odometry, so the robot knows its pose on the map                                                                                      |
| **Navigator**                  | Plans a path on the map's occupancy grid and drives the base along it, avoiding obstacles, until the goal is reached                                                                                              |
| **Visual odometry** (optional) | Estimates odometry from the camera, for robots without wheel odometry such as walking robots                                                                                                                      |
| **Map bundle** (`.nav`)        | One file with the map (point cloud and occupancy grid) and the localizer and navigator settings for one site ([Load and Configure a Map](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/navigation/map_bundle/index.md)) |

By default the localizer works in the plane: it estimates x, y and heading on the map. There is one localizer and one navigator per Station, so one robot per Station navigates.

______________________________________________________________________

## 2. Coordinate Frames

| Frame                | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                               |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `map`                | The fixed frame of the site: x and y horizontal, z up, the floor at z = 0, in meters. The point cloud, the grid, the initial pose and goals use it.                                   |
| `odom`               | The odometry frame: continuous motion measured by Strider's wheel odometry or by Visual odometry. It drifts slowly, for example as the wheels slip; the localizer corrects the drift. |
| `base_link`          | The robot, **on the floor** below its center: x forward, y left, z up                                                                                                                 |
| Camera optical frame | The camera (for example `cam0_optical`): x right, y down, z forward along the view                                                                                                    |

```
flowchart TB
    M["map"] -- "Localizer<br>(drift correction)" --> O["odom"]
    O -- "odometry<br>(Strider or Visual odometry)" --> B["base_link<br>(on the floor)"]
    B -- "extrinsics.yaml<br>(fixed)" --> C["cam0_optical<br>(x right, y down, z forward)"]
```

The localizer publishes the correction `map → odom`; Strider (or Visual odometry) publishes `odom → base_link`; the map bundle's extrinsics give `base_link → camera`.

Because the localizer is planar by default (`icp.planar: true`) and holds the height, roll and pitch of `base_link` at zero, `base_link` lies on the floor.

Because `base_link` is on the floor, the camera's mounting height in the extrinsics is its height **above the floor**, not above the robot's body frame. Measure the camera's x and y from the base origin that your odometry tracks, but its z from the floor, even when your robot model places `base_link` higher, for example at the wheel axles. A height taken from a raised base puts every camera point too low by that offset: the fit error exceeds `icp.max_rmse`, and the localization status stays **Initializing** (`initializing`).

______________________________________________________________________

## 3. Set Up Navigation

| Step                                                                                            | Where                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1. Drive the base with Strider                                                                  | [Quick Start](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/get_started/quick_start/index.md)                                                                                                                       |
| 2. Add a camera gateway and check its image                                                     | [Cameras and IMUs](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/gateways/sensors_and_cameras/index.md)                                                                                                             |
| 3. Prepare the map bundle of the site                                                           | [Create a Map from Your Site](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/navigation/create_map/index.md), or use a finished bundle                                                                               |
| 4. Add the Localizer and the Navigator, upload the map once to the Localizer, connect the ports | [Load and Configure a Map](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/navigation/map_bundle/index.md), [Navigate in Simulation](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/navigation/simulation_tutorial/index.md) |
| 5. Set the initial pose and send goals                                                          | [Strider › Navigation Page](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/controllers/strider/#5-navigation-page)                                                                                                   |

The connections:

| From (requires)          | To (provides)                                      |
| ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------- |
| Localizer `camera`       | Camera gateway `camera`                            |
| Localizer `odometry`     | Strider `odometry` (or Visual odometry `odometry`) |
| Navigator `localization` | Localizer `localization`                           |
| Navigator `map`          | Localizer `map`                                    |
| Navigator `mobile_base`  | Strider `mobile_base`                              |

Start the nodes in this order: gateway, Strider, camera gateway, localizer, navigator. The localizer needs a running camera and an uploaded map; the navigator needs the map bundle's navigator settings.

______________________________________________________________________

## 4. Localization States

| State                   | Meaning                                                                   | What to do                                                 |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Uninitialized**       | No pose yet                                                               | Set the initial pose                                       |
| **Initializing**        | Searching around the initial pose                                         | Wait; keep the robot still                                 |
| **Healthy** (localized) | The camera view matches the map                                           | Navigate                                                   |
| **Degraded**            | Few recent matches (for example a featureless area or many people around) | Goals are still accepted; check the camera view            |
| **Lost**                | No match for a long time; the navigator stops                             | Set the initial pose again, or use **Global localization** |
| **Relocalizing**        | A new initial pose is being checked                                       | Wait                                                       |

**Global localization** on Strider's Navigation page searches the whole map for the robot's pose. Stop the robot before you start it, review the best candidate, and apply it.

______________________________________________________________________

## 5. Settings

The localizer and the navigator share their settings with the map bundle. Edit them in the inspector of either node under **NAVIGATION SETTINGS** (or with **Settings** on the node card), while the localizer, the navigator and visual odometry are stopped. The most useful ones:

| Group        | Setting                                            | Meaning                                                                                                            |
| ------------ | -------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Navigator    | `FollowPath.desired_linear_vel`                    | Cruise speed (m/s)                                                                                                 |
|              | `max_angular_vel`, `rotate_to_heading_angular_vel` | Turning speeds (rad/s)                                                                                             |
|              | `rotate_to_heading_min_angle`                      | Above this heading error (rad), the robot turns in place before it drives. Use a small value for skid-steer bases. |
|              | `xy_goal_tolerance`, `yaw_goal_tolerance`          | How close counts as reached (m, rad)                                                                               |
|              | `robot_radius`, `inflation_radius`                 | Robot size and the clearance kept from obstacles (m)                                                               |
| Localizer    | `icp.max_jump_m`, `icp.max_jump_rad`               | Largest correction accepted per update                                                                             |
|              | `sensor.depth_min`, `sensor.depth_max`             | Depth range of the camera used for matching (m)                                                                    |
| Initial pose | `x`, `y`, `yaw`                                    | The pose used when no other pose is known                                                                          |

Uploading a map bundle again replaces these settings with the bundle's. The full list is in [Map Bundle Format](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/navigation/map_bundle_format/#files); from the SSH workspace use `sodero navigation get` and `sodero navigation apply` ([sodero CLI](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/ssh_workspace/sodero_cli/index.md)).

______________________________________________________________________

## 6. Send Goals from Programs

| From          | How                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Strider       | **Set Goal**, **Start Navigation** ([Strider](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/controllers/strider/#5-navigation-page))                                                                         |
| SSH workspace | `sodero tools call navigation.navigate_to_pose`, `navigation.get_status`, `navigation.cancel_navigation`, `localization.set_initial_pose`                                                              |
| Your module   | A module connected to the Navigator's `navigation` port; it can send goals and follow their progress ([Create Custom Modules](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/extend/custom_modules/index.md)) |

A goal is a pose in the `map` frame. A patrol is a sequence of goals sent one after another by your program.

# Create a Map from Your Site

Stellar Station does not build maps on the robot; there is no SLAM. You make the map bundle of your site beforehand, from a 3D model or a 3D scan of the site, and then upload it as described in [Load and Configure a Map](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/navigation/map_bundle/index.md). Every file and key of the bundle is specified in [Map Bundle Format](https://docs.sodero.io/stellar-x/v2.0.0/navigation/map_bundle_format/index.md).

The Localizer matches the camera's depth images against the 3D point cloud of the bundle to find the robot on the map. The Navigator plans paths on the 2D occupancy grid. Both describe the same site in the same coordinates.
